notes.title: House Traditions and winning paths
notes.content:
Oy, rulers!

Traditions are one of the cornerstones of your House in the game. In this devblog, we'll look at their depth and importance for your nobles and progression.

[h3]The Role of House Traditions[/h3]

In Calderia, all Houses choose their Traditions, which are their core values that will influence the type of relationships with other Houses and their playstyle. Traditions influence politics and every interaction, this will require sacrifice and pondering your choices between choosing the best outcome of an event or staying true to your Traditions.

Traditions weigh on your decisions, whether you prefer to prioritize your family's benefits or your own goals on the short term. From the game's early concepts, Traditions have been central to your family and fiefdom by allowing you to unlock actions, units, bonuses, and even winning paths.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/0abe6574d890008f7b23817ee60a5ed64ade7cf9.png[/img]

[h3]Tradition Tree[/h3]

During playtests, we introduced the Tradition tree. Traditions can affect the way you play and win the game. For example, Peacemakers need worse relations before anyone can declare war on them, while Warriors excel in military conflicts.

Traditions are divided into six categories, paired to oppose each other: Warriors vs. Scholars, Idealists vs. Schemers, and Isolationists vs. Peacemakers. Advancing in one Tradition blocks the opposing tradition, so choose your Traditions wisely! Houses with opposing Traditions may naturally despise each other because of them. Starting near Warrior Houses differs from starting near Isolationist neighbors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/34d0288646dc7141d0ebfe614c8e18b42be815f2.png[/img]

[h3]Earning Tradition Points[/h3]

Events and conflicts award tradition points, which can be general or specific to your chosen tradition. Specific choices in events also earn tradition points. For instance, Schemers might pursue shady deals, while Idealists avoid them. Choices aligning with your traditions earn more points.

Going against your traditions is possible but comes with penalties, including losing Traditions points and, therefore, hurting your progress for the next Tradition node. Such decisions hinder your Tradition's development, making it harder to compete with other Houses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/3a6c0d6aa5bf9d720af24e82ede33679fbfcafad.png[/img]

[h3]Traditions & Winning Paths[/h3]

During Early Access, we've added over 25 traditions and two winning paths:
[list]
[*] [b]Scholarly Path:[/b] A peaceful scheming option using Schemers and Scholars traditions. This playstyle focuses on diplomacy and building a network of schools across fiefdoms.
[*] [b]Isolationist Path:[/b] A war-focused path using Warriors and Isolationists traditions. This path is for those who prefer independence from the Empire and hermit-style gameplay.
[/list]
Each path unlocks unique bonuses, delegations, actions, and new units or companions through tradition nodes in the Tradition Tree menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/f46fd950583f92b8138933dafb7e8856f5f12123.png[/img]

Thank you for reading, and we are extremely grateful for your support and contribution since the release in 1.0!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: New demo!
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

[b]Ship to the land of Calderia in our new demo![/b]

Rise to power as the most influential House in this bountiful land, guiding your nobles through the feudal ranks to rule Calderia. Use diplomacy, trade, schemes, and warfare to achieve your goals and build a lasting legacy of power.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/18e44b52f92067eaf3439b8abbfd3da8f1ed3d8b.gif[/img]

[h3]Download the demo on the Steam page![/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812910/Great_Houses_of_Calderia/

Learn more about the world of Calderia and the wide range of choices you can make in the demo!

[h3]You will be able to:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Create your noble House and family
[*] Create your coat of arms
[*] Choose your family traditions
[*] Discover the world of Calderia
[*] Play the first 2 years of your rule
[*] Manage your fiefdom
[*] Develop relations with the Houses
[*] Trade, raise an army, declare war, arrange marriages and scheme against your Houses
[/list]
The demo lasts about 30 minutes to 1 hour of gameplay, but you can replay it as many times as you want. Create new Houses with different character traits and House traditions, try various strategies, and unlock new companions and military units!

Ascend Calderia's ranks, create your noble family!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: Making and customizing your House and characters
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

First and foremost, we thank you for your feedback ever since we launched the game in 1.0. We are focusing on improving the game, adding content, and fixing issues thanks to your contributions. [b]Regular updates are coming up[/b], and your comments help us in this process.

Other topics for today, we're part of the [b]Steam Endless Replayability Fest[/b] (May 13–20)! And we have [b]Trading cards[/b] that have just been approved by Steam! We figured it would be a good opportunity to talk about [b]customization[/b], shall we?


[h3]House Creation[/h3]

In our game, the foundations of your tale as a ruler begin with the creation of your noble House.
[list]
[*] [b]Tradition Selection:[/b] You'll choose a Tradition for your House, a defining aspect that influences your bonuses and gameplay style. Whether you embrace the fearless spirit of the Warriors, the wisdom of Scholars, the artfulness of Schemers, the togetherness of Peacemakers, the seclusive nature of Isolationists, or the prosperity of Idealists, your Tradition will shape your path.
[*] [b]Starting Adult Nobles:[/b] Your journey begins with the selection of four randomized starting adult nobles. Each character comes with their own unique set of traits and skills, shaping their capabilities and predispositions when you will manage them and assign them tasks. You can randomize the characters as much as you want to get the perfect (or worst) family! When creating your House, you will have to designate the Head of House, this character will have more responsibility and will have special delegations for the Empire.
[*] [b]Coat of Arms:[/b] With your noble roster assembled, you'll have the opportunity to design your House's distinctive coat of arms. This emblem is the visual representation of your lineage and can be customized to reflect your style and personality.
[*] [b]Region Selection:[/b] Every corner of the land of Calderia offers its own advantages and challenges in terms of resource production. Choose wisely as you select the region where your House will settle, as it will influence your strategic decisions and the progression of your House.
[*] [b]Difficulty Settings:[/b] This is a new addition brought with the 1.0 update. Tailor the challenge to your liking with 3 difficulty settings. Whether you seek to rule and explore the world and atmosphere of Calderia or a grueling test of your rule, there's a difficulty level suited to your ambitions.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/8f960e6beaf0247d4f48c77b90698129e340c54a.png[/img]


[h3]Character Customization[/h3]

In addition to shaping the foundations of your House, you'll be able to personalize the appearance and name of your noble characters through our character customization feature if you want.
[list]
[*] [b]Portrait Customization:[/b] Alter the appearance of your nobles with a diverse array of options for hair, headwear, clothing, and backgrounds. From regal finery to battle-worn armor, customize your characters to reflect Calderian fashion, their roles, or personalities within your House.
[/list]Portraits can be changed for any character at any moment after creating your House by clicking on the quill icon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/e976ecf94f0a0f6b7f24858b46e1fdb2c1ede6f3.png[/img]


[h3]Steam Trading Cards[/h3]

Some of you requested them, and we're happy to let you know that Steam recently approved our Trading cards, and they are [b]now available[/b]! These collectible cards feature stunning illustrations from the world of our game, allowing you to personalize your Steam profile and showcase your love for the Mediterranean Renaissance and the fictional world we made inspired by this era.

You can read more information about them [url=https://steamcommunity.com/tradingcards/]here[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/23c7db6692a3a85786f476212d33dae314e9bbe5.png[/img]

Thank you for joining us on this journey. Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to expand and refine Great Houses of Calderia with you!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: The seeds of the Civil War
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

As you know, we released the Civil War feature recently with the 1.0 update. We wanted to thank you for your feedback and support ever since. All the details and insights you share with us are extremely useful. There were issues with the Civil War, and know that we're doing our best to fix them as quickly as possible.

In today's devblog, we'd like to explore the concept and the ideas behind the [b]Civil War[/b].

[h3]Tainted soil[/h3]

Since the birth of the game idea and its very first drafts, which we later named Great Houses of Calderia, we've always envisioned a climactic finale, like a "big bang," fueled by rivalries and the thirst for power. This endgame is meant to give weight to the decisions you made throughout your rule. When the game draws to a close, the fate of your characters—be they brave or cowardly, their histories and personalities—will determine your performance in the events to come. We named this end of an era the "Civil War", though it leans more towards rebellion or a fight for independence, depending on how it unfolds. Unlike the unity seen in the American Revolutionary War, where colonists stood together against the British, in Calderia, loyalties are divided, with some favoring allegiance to the empire and others yearning for Calderian independence.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/291886ff8dc648c4222b6aa5c98b4b50ba55b63c.png[/img]

[h3]Crimson rivers[/h3]

So the Civil War begins, gradually gaining momentum throughout the midgame while all the Houses pick their sides. The Emperor makes a grand entrance into the picture, and we catch glimpses of Calderia's Houses reclaiming their ancestral lands and the forgotten knowledge of the previous civilization. In other words, the Empire embodies medieval times, whereas Calderia inspires to go forward. This dualism now reveals more about where part of the inspiration for the game came from. Europe was transitioning from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance and then the Enlightenment, but when the world is changing, there are progressive forces and regressive forces, those who push for advancement and those who are resisting and in danger of losing something in the process. And all that change usually causes conflicts. While these struggles often arise from within, in Great Houses of Calderia, they are externalized through the entities of the Empire and Emperor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/6e0d20d68d122d2b5d68be3010681951c3742081.jpg[/img]

[h3]Roots for the future[/h3]

In essence, the Civil War in the game adds a deeper purpose and weight to your decisions. You have the freedom to embrace the old traditions or the new, the progress, and shape the kind of Calderia you wish to see. This also injects a sense of urgency into the gameplay and narrative. With other Houses also competing for power, if you aim to influence the future, you need to act fast! Strive to rise in the ranks and become a key player in the final conflict, or risk being manipulated as a mere pawn in others' schemes. Your path could lead to independence or even to becoming the Emperor's right-hand as the Viceroy, if you will.

During the Civil War, the Emperor will deploy vast armies to defend the rule of his lands while leading unique and exclusive units for his faction. A Calderian victory is impossible until the Emperor is cast out, you have to overthrow his forces. However, the Calderian side for independence must ultimately prevail in the overall conflict for the war to conclude in a victory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/820873ba80a5f5884f3b9ae00f81b26e1d1c8ace.jpg[/img]

For the making and unfolding of the Civil War, a lot of tradition features have also been developed while keeping in mind the various playstyle choices and how they would play out in the Civil War. In the 1.0 update, we introduced a wealth of new content centered around the Civil War feature. Starting with the event prompting you to choose your allegiance amidst the chaos of war. With eight distinct main pathways leading to various conclusions and an additional thirteen minor variations building up to various outcomes of the Civil War. The Emperor commands six exclusive units, leading his faction into battle. Thirty new events related to the Civil War and three unique war types with a set of unique illustrations were added to the narrative of the Civil War. The Main Path to Victory has been finalized, alongside the Isolationist Path, providing alternative routes to success.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/741426cdb4dfc035d5fe24cdf9535db2e5b0c921.jpg[/img]

And that concludes our devblog on the Civil War. We really value your feedback on this feature, the difficulty settings, the AI, the balance, and all the additions we've made. Thank you for being part of the journey and for your contribution!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: 1.0 Release and a word from the team
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

[h3]Great Houses of Calderia is now in 1.0![/h3]

Watch the full release trailer:
[previewyoutube=6qeo6Yp2qg4;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]A word from the team[/h2]

It's been quite a journey so far since the Early Access release last year. We've been developing and crafting the game alongside you, thanks to your feedback. We like to say that a video game is an organic product that evolves not only with the people who make it but also with its community. We are extremely grateful and thrilled by your support and commitment to making the best version of the game.

As the game is releasing in 1.0, comes one of the biggest features: the [b]Civil War[/b]. We've been hard at work designing, coding, illustrating, and testing this big chunk that represents the late game. We are preparing a devblog to introduce its content. We want to keep expanding the game and its content with your support.

Now that the game is in 1.0, we are still committed to assessing your constructive comments and incorporating your ideas into future updates. [b]Thank you[/b] once again for your support, and your continuous contributions to the development of Great Houses of Calderia.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/6dc6eb3ec9a06c827577bb5750479240ba167625.jpg[/img]

[h2]What changed during Early Access?[/h2]

The game is now much more dense and challenging with your contribution. In our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1812910/announcements/detail/4173223997939831069][b]latest Monthly Development Update[/b][/url], we shared the [b]biggest additions and improvements[/b] made during Early Access. We’ve been hard at work to prepare for the 1.0, many features have been refined with your help: more events, Siege mechanic, Military overhaul, Bandits and safety, character skill training, World map and map modes (filters), new winning paths, character appearance customization, AI and UI improvements, overall balance, and more!
https://steamcommunity.com/games/1812910/announcements/detail/4173223997939831069

You can read [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1812910/view/4216008828232832153][b]1.0 update patch note[/b][/url] with all the details regarding the Civil War, overall balance, and other changes!

notes.title: April Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

It’s the final stretch before the 1.0 release! We’re working on all the final tweaks and tests to prepare for the update. Before you can explore the new content, let’s take a look back at [b]some of the biggest changes[/b] made during Early Access. We cannot stress enough [b]how impactful your feedback is[/b] to us, and we encourage you to keep sharing them to help us improve the game!


[h2]Biggest Early Access features[/h2]

[h3]Civil War[/h3]
This addition coming with the [b]1.0 update[/b] will please the community, as it gives much more purpose and deeper meaning to your decisions, while adding a significant twist to the [b]late game[/b]. It starts by slowly building up over the midgame while you and different Houses progressively [b]choose sides[/b]. You can decide whether to embrace the old or the modern, as well as the kind of Calderia you desire. This also adds to the game's sense of urgency. Other Houses are also moving forward, so if you want to be among those who shape the future, you must hurry! Try to rise in the ranks so that you may be one of the primary actors in the end-of-war conflict, rather than a pawn in other people's games. During the Civil War, the Emperor would send out large armies to defend his rule over the lands, with the army composed of troops that are entirely unique to the Emperor. This conflict cannot end with a Calderian victory before the Emperor is cast out, and the Calderian side must also win the overall conflict. We have been designing tradition features and perks with your various playstyle preferences in mind, as well as how they will play out during the Civil War.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/78dbaf16cdb5c53179cec52dc65aa2f02b3ad7df.png[/img]

[h3]Traditions & Winning paths[/h3]
During Early Access, we progressively added [b]over 25 Traditions[/b] and [b]two alternative winning paths[/b] to complete the game.
[list]
[*] The first one, the [b]Scholarly path[/b], is a more peaceful and scheming option using both Schemers and Scholars Traditions. This playstyle is for those who wish to build rather than fight. It is still heavily involved in politics with other Houses, and relies on good diplomatic relations with others to spread your network of schools to their fiefdoms. So it allows you to build something for other fiefdoms, giving them improvements, starting by building your own School of Wisdom for your Fiefdom.
[*] The second, the [b]Isolationist path[/b], relies more on war and seeks independence from the Empire, it combines Warriors and Isolationists Traditions. You abandon the idea of a unified Calderia and will much rather rule a smaller part alone and be left alone. So this winning path is for those who prefer to play more hermit-style gameplay and keep both enemies and friends away.
[/list] To make these paths, we designed and implemented a handful of Tradition nodes in the Traditions Tree menu which unlocks various bonuses like: unique delegations and actions, additional points in war or social conflicts, new units or companions, for example.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/43c76b99e1dec1fe73826cd55f2ede32d41aefb3.png[/img]

[h3]Character customization[/h3]
In September, we added this feature for more freedom on your nobles’ creation. You can [b]rename and customize your characters’ appearance[/b] with a set of portrait parts (head, hair, clothing, background) when you create your House and at any other moment in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/74e50499401b867fca5b0a3c2244694cf92aa8ff.png[/img]

[h3]Bandits, safety, & map events[/h3]
In December, we implemented Bandits and the Safety features. This addition led to the appearance of bandits on the roads of the world map. They appear if your fiefdom’s safety is not high enough. No path is as safe as it used to be for merchants and soldiers. This feature came with a series of brand [b]new and unique events[/b] you’ll have to deal with when they appear. With your help, we balanced how bandits attack fiefdoms and the way AI handles them. Bandits used to attack you too often and affected the beginning of your rule by starting their raids quickly after you created your fiefdom. To make sure that you had the time to prepare for them, we made a few changes: fiefdom starting set to 2 (instead of 0), preventing bandits from sieging repeatedly, and adding more outcomes, choices, and dynamic costs to bandits delegations and events.

[h3]Siege[/h3]
The Siege feature, as well as the military unit overhaul, have made [b]war more complex and strategic[/b]. We gradually introduced the Siege feature in December. For this mechanic, we added perks to some building upgrades, affecting both siege duration and speed. Attacking the city of a fiefdom at war will start a siege. When besieged, the defender must establish a garrison (without the expense of forming an army, although upkeep is still required). With your help, we introduced the ability to adapt your garrison to match the approaching army. The attacking army begins constructing siege equipment and, when completed, attempts to invade the fiefdom. The siege tower symbol shows the progress of the siege equipment. While under siege, the defending army loses health, and all production and trade resources are temporarily halted. The defense may try to lift the siege at any moment. To improve the clarity and information regarding siege, we worked on the garrison view UI and tooltips. The AI has been tweaked so that it handles sieges much more effectively and is less likely to lack defensive forces. We also created an event for when a siege begins without defense to provide information.

[h3]War and military units[/h3]
February was busy with the [b]rework of the military units[/b] thanks to your constructive criticism. We focused on improving the new military unit logic. While the battle system will remain fundamentally unchanged (a mini-game with a board and soldiers to manage), we have worked to make it more exciting and tactical. We chose to make battles and social conflicts (negotiations) completely skippable when we published the game in Early Access in August. If you aren't keen on playing the mini-games, you are free to select your units as well as the objectives and outcomes that are most relevant to you before clicking the "auto-resolve" option.
[b]You can read more about the changes we made in this devblog:[/b]
https://steamcommunity.com/games/1812910/announcements/detail/7356139324008352974


[h2]Player-based additions highlight[/h2]

[h3]Difficulty settings, AI & Balancing[/h3]
Balancing the game proved to be challenging, with the more experienced members of the community finding it too easy in the end game, while newcomers faced the intended level of challenge. So, also with the 1.0 update, to adapt to various skills and experiences, we kept improving AI behavior and will implement [b]three difficulty levels[/b]: Apprentice, Bourgeois, and Maester. Apprentice AI operates the same as before, AI manages production and worker efficiency slightly less effectively than you. Bourgeois AI maintains efficiency when moving workers and receives a small production boost. Maester AI, similar to Bourgeois, enjoys a larger production bonus and a head start with the buildings. To compensate, we've made the economy more challenging. We advise less experienced players to start with an easy fiefdom and Apprentice AI. We've reduced production bonuses and adjusted food production to 2.5 per farmer instead of 3. Building upgrades are now considerably cheaper, with costs remaining stable across levels and fewer resource requirements. Traditions have also been made more accessible. Your save files have been invaluable in these adjustments, providing crucial insights. Thank you for your continued support and feedback!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/7bd6edc4f7d54e5d1a12e55bec2a09e4b102388b.png[/img]

[h3]Character skill training[/h3]
In March, we added one of your suggestions: the ability to train your characters to improve their skills (Diplomacy, Economy, Intrigue, or Military), one level at a time. The duration of the training depends on the skill level, the higher the skill, the longer it will take to improve it. Based on your feedback, we've adjusted the skill Exp. distribution to narrow the gain gap between training and other tasks by respectively reducing training Exp. and boosting Exp. from the other tasks. Skill training is considered a task, this means characters won’t be able to undertake additional ones while training, and it cancels their current assignment. Upon reaching a new skill level, the training automatically ends. To initiate training, navigate to your Fiefdom's Diplomacy menu and select the desired skill category. Additionally, we've introduced a Character skill preview accessible via the Left ALT button in Settings > Input Settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/101076cdef1bea03d7aba6d013e7a7b61cbbcfe6.png[/img]

[h3]UI and map filters (“modes”)[/h3]
UI has been an important part of the game and feedback. We’ve added many tooltips and icons, [b]improved the tutorial[/b] for the 1.0, and the map clarity with filters (modes), while adding clearer army icons to identify allies and enemies better. These modes provide critical knowledge by activating them and clicking on each region, such as the relationships between Heads of House, and we added the ability to view unmarried characters using this map option. It is also possible to examine each House's feudal status (vassals and lieges), resources, spies recruited, ongoing wars (and who is at war with whom), and alliances. We've implemented an active map mode indicator for better clarity and as a reminder. For the “Resource” mode, you can select multiple resources from a window that opens above the map mode toggle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/f5e2902e626ee2227381c89414cede8ea3408c38.png[/img]

[h3]Optimization & memory leak fixes[/h3]
We have been testing and improving the optimization of the world map, its textures, and the simultaneous events happening on the map and for all the Houses. Thanks to your reports and save files, we were able to investigate and fix the issues and calculations which led to crashes.


The 1.0 update is just a few days away! We can't wait to hear your feedback on the Civil War, the difficulty settings, and all the features we refined over the course of Early Access. Thank you for being part of the journey and for your help!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: Full release on May 2!
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

We will soon launch in 1.0 after almost 10 months in Early Access!

[h3]On May 2, Great Houses of Calderia will release in 1.0![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/46ee3f6ed934bd1794ba89556f80a3c562c8ca9b.gif[/img]

[b]Thank you[/b] for your [b]support[/b] and [b]feedback[/b] throughout Early Access. We hope you are as thrilled as we are about the launch date, which is just two weeks away!

As you may have noticed, we released fewer updates for Great Houses of Calderia over the past few months. You now know the reason why, we've been busy working on this [b]new update[/b] for the game: the [b]1.0 release[/b]!

[h2]Early Access ending soon![/h2]

Since February, we've been focused on [b]enhancing the content[/b] for the 1.0 update to make sure that the game is ready for its official release.

Everything is being tested, refined, and validated, from new tutorials to balancing and polishing, implementing the last Traditions nodes, improving AI behavior, UI clarity, and pushing stability and optimization fixes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/1d7cb2d4a8399f5222fe147128e396ac0a93a6d4.png[/img]

Throughout the Early Access phase, we added [b]new mechanics[/b] and [b]improved[/b] the [b]newly implemented[/b] and [b]existing features[/b]: Siege, Military overhaul, Bandits and safety, added more events, some of which are on the map, character training skills, World map and map modes (filters), new winning paths, character appearance customization, the chronicle, and more adjustments thanks to your comments!

You can read all our previous [b]Monthly Development Updates[/b] we have published until now:
[list]
[*] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1812910/announcements/detail/4197991893252994073]March Development Update[/url]
[*] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1812910/announcements/detail/4138316032665479893]February Development Update[/url]

[h2]Civil War feature[/h2]

Speaking of the full release, the [b]Civil War feature[/b] will be available on that date! We're preparing a [b]devblog[/b] on this feature to explain how it will work. Calderia will soon be torn and set on fire. We can't wait for you to try out this new feature and be the architect of the fate of Calderia!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/40ef6898da105cee8927d2167adbcece3f0e6c35.png[/img]

notes.title: March Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,
 
This month has been characterized by extensive [b]behind-the-scenes efforts[/b]. Primarily, our focus has been on advancing the [b]Civil War feature[/b]. We'll expand more on it in this post, and even more so in a dedicated devblog later this month. This feature holds significant importance for the late game.

In addition to the Civil War, we've been considering and implementing features based on your feedback. Furthermore, we've been improving existing features, UI, fixing bugs and issues. Your insights are greatly appreciated, and we encourage you to keep sharing them to help us improve the game! And now, let's move on to exploring the changes that have been made this month!

[h2]Design & Balancing[/h2]

[b]Civil War:[/b] As mentioned above, we are still working hard on the Civil War. That late part of the game will be completed and should be fully playable around the end of April. Progress this month includes additional interfaces and screens to depict the rise of this dramatic timeline, in addition to a series of unique events and new battlefields triggered during the civil war up to the end of the game. We are currently implementing, testing, and polishing this feature, so stay tuned!

[b]AI:[/b] A lot of work has been done on the AI behavior, especially for early game, where it will be better at setting up and developing its fiefdom. We’ve been focusing on this aspect a lot lately, and we’d love to have your [b]feedback[/b] (and [b]save files[/b]) on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1812910/discussions/0/4358994946502213214/][b]Steam[/b][/url], or [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord[/url] to keep on improving AI!

[b]Military overhaul:[/b] Early March, we implemented the military overhaul. You can read more about how it changed the way military conflicts work in this [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1812910/view/7356139324008352973][b]devblog[/b][/url].

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1812910/view/7356139324008352973

[b]Delegations:[/b] We’ve been fixing a few issues regarding delegation conditions, some were too strict, making them rare. A set of new delegations has been added related to Traditions in the latest update in March. Also, in some cases, the character you decided to court was on a trade delegation, which led to a lot of waiting until the first date happened because of the trade. Since trading is the only continuous delegation in the game, we made it impossible to court someone who's handling a trade to avoid that issue. Regarding trade, an important fix was made thanks to you. Trade delegations are now canceled if one of the Houses does not have enough resources for one trip.

[b]Character training skills:[/b] This was a suggestion from you, the community! You can now assign a task to your characters to improve their skills (one level and one type at a time, i.e.: Diplomacy, Economy, Intrigue, and Military). The higher the skill level, the longer it takes to increase it. This training improves the skills at a slightly faster rate than other actions. It is considered a task, and your characters won't be able to do another while they are training. This means that it also cancels your character's current assigned task. Whenever the skill level increases, the task is automatically finished.
To do so, head over to your own Fiefdom's Diplomacy menu to start the training in Diplomacy, Intrigue, Military, and Economy. We also added a Character skill preview accessible by pressing the Left ALT button (Settings > Input Settings).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/8dac6b2948046bcc7c1412970d330b93e875590f.png[/img]

[b]Traditions:[/b] A set of new traditions have been implemented:
[list]
[*] « Strongest Among Giants » of the Warrior path (which prevents your military units from panicking and improves their survivability)
[*] « Whose Land, Their Rules » of the Isolationist path (which forces passing caravans to give you 5% of their content)
[*] « King of Hearts » of the Peacemaker path (which unlocks 2 unique delegations)
[*] « Always Pay Back Debt » of the Idealist path (which unlocks a unique delegation and gives the ability to make a House be in debt to you).
[/list] And with them, more than a dozen new events related to specific Traditions have been added.

[b]Siege:[/b] New iterations were led this month on this feature, along with UI improvements. We’ve added a set of new buttons: Assault and Sally Out (in Garrison view, to attack out of a sieged castle). The Siege slowdown changed to wall upgrades from castle upgrades, and its duration text is visible in the Production View.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/8f93c496fc69ee3c03b472b446b656baef8ef71b.png[/img]

[h2]Visuals & Interface[/h2]

[b]World map:[/b] Map clarity and mode improvements that work as filters, including clearer army icons to identify allies and enemies better. In “Resource” mode, you can now select multiple resources from a window that opens above the map mode toggle.

[b]UI:[/b] The windowed interface now has fade in-out effect. Various fixes were made to the interface, from tooltips, to information clarity, missing icons and text wrapping. New notifications and tooltips have been added.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/f8ca80c119215e208c9aa004f474abeb07d51577.png[/img]

[h2]Technical fixes & optimization[/h2]

[b]Crash:[/b] If you experience a crash, please send the crash report via the Unreal Engine Crash Report window, and let us know on Discord or in the Steam forums.

[h3]For more information, read the full aggregated patch notes below:[/h3]

[b]Added[/b]
[list]
[*] Tradition - Strongest Among Giants
[*] Tradition - Whose Lands His Rules
[*] Tradition - King of Hearts
[*] Tradition - Always Pay Back Debt
[*] AI is now able to check resource status in its plan as a condition for action
[*] 10+ new events, mostly relating to Traditions
[*] 10 new playgrounds
[*] 5 new winning conditions to playgrounds
[*] 6 new delegations
[*] UI fade animations
[*] Siege - Assault button 
[*] Siege - Sally Out button to Garrison view - can attack out of sieged castle
[*] Clicking on the Resource bar buttons should take you to the corresponding profession
[*] Characters can train skills at home via the Diplomacy menu
[*] Character skill preview by pressing Left ALT button (Settings > Input Settings)

notes.title: Military unit rework
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

In our latest update, we've implemented a significant [b]overhaul of military units[/b]. Our primary goal was to provide clearer and more tactical roles for each unit. It was [b]driven by your feedback[/b], and we really appreciate the comments you shared with us.

[h2]Military unit rework[/h2]

One of the biggest changes is the revision of the [b]"good against"[/b] logic for military units. Units 
armor is now a much more important part of their unit type, as it is compared to weapons they are attacked with. Before, units wielded weapons that dealt extra damage against specific unit types. Now, units also have [b]armor types[/b] (Light, Medium, and Heavy) and some attacks are more efficient against specific armor types. For example, Crossbows deal increased damage against Light and Medium Infantry, and Light and Medium Cavalry. For example, Light Infantry has light armor and Heavy Cavalry has heavy armor. This change adds depth to unit interactions and encourages you to consider your [b]army compositions[/b] carefully.

Additionally, we've introduced short descriptions accompanied by lore snippets for military units and extra information for unit icons to provide a quick [b]overview[/b] of each unit's type. These tooltips provide insight into a unit's capabilities and backstory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/0d24f94c68bc85ddfec938c1e072b2968cab5158.jpg[/img]

[h2]More specificities and rules[/h2]

In addition to the categorization and weapon adjustments, we've implemented several tactical improvements. Ranged attacks now have [b]varying ranges[/b], which makes positioning and unit composition more impactful. For example, the Calderian Fire used by Ignis Iaculatores has a range of 2, while catapults boast an unlimited range.

We've also introduced [b]special rules[/b] for certain units to increase their [b]survivability[/b] or [b]effectiveness[/b] in combat. Healing units, like the Ordo Vita unit, can tend wounds to keep your army alive. Ordo Fortis, on the other hand, can bolster the morale of your units with their activated ability Rally Troops. Shields now reduce incoming ranged damage for units like Swordsmen, Armigeri, and Ordo Fortis, while Pikemen benefit from the Long Reach special, increasing their defense in melee combat.

Armor has been reworked to provide more survivability, particularly against ranged attacks. This change ensures that armored units remain viable and impactful on the battlefield.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/19a5dbe22958cb2a68d10996d738af907adede05.jpg[/img]

[h3]"Bonus against" examples[/h3]
Indicators for the arrow up and arrow down indicate if a unit has a special rule against another. This still does not mean they are ultimately good or bad in their matchup. For example: Poleaxer (Tier I) has attack 2.0 / defense 1.5. City Guard (Tier II) has attack 2.0 / defense 3.0 with their medium armor.

Poleaxe special ability allows 50% bonus attack against medium and heavy armor, effectively giving the Poleaxer unit attack 3.0 against City Guard. Sounds dangerous for the City Guard, but they still beat the defense value of Poleaxers and have higher morale and health values. City Guard will win the one-on-one match but will suffer about 50% of their health damage in the process.


[h2]Unit roles and economy balancing[/h2]

With these changes, the tempo of military conflicts has shifted as some units have gained increased resilience. We'd love to know [b]your opinion[/b] on how these changes have affected the [b]flow of military combat[/b]. Deploying the correct units in the right place to capitalize on their strengths effectively is key to prevailing on the battlefield.

We've also introduced units with [b]bonus damage[/b] against specific armor types, representing their weapons' capability to minimize the effectiveness of opposing armor. For example, Ignis Iaculatores' Calderian Fire deals bonus damage against medium and heavy armor, making it particularly effective against heavily armored foes. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/302b9576835a7188771d2e23dac0809d5318f9d2.jpg[/img]

Furthermore, we've adjusted [b]unit tiers[/b] and their [b]unlock conditions[/b] to provide a more balanced progression system. All unit stats and economic aspects are subject to further rebalancing as we gather feedback and conduct additional testing internally.

[h3]Some unit role examples[/h3]
Ignis Iaculatores is our glass cannon anti-armour unit, but its short range and lack of armouring make it vulnerable to opposing long-range fire.
Knights are armed with lances and are especially good against heavy infantry and heavy cavalry. Again, they hurt everyone else too, but they are well-equipped against other heavily armoured combatants.
Pikemen excel at holding ground in melee, especially against cavalry, but are prone to crossbow fire. Their medium armor allows them to still ignore extra damage from normal bows.

[h3]Economy balancing[/h3]
Rough guidelines for resource values as gold equivalent. These values will likely evolve as we keep balancing the game.

[table]
    [tr]
        [th]Tier[/th]
        [th]Upkeep[/th]
        [th]Raise cost[/th]
    [/tr]
  [tr]
        [td]I[/td]
        [td]0.5-1[/td]
        [td]50-100[/td]
    [/tr]
  [tr]
        [td]II[/td]
        [td]1-2[/td]
        [td]100-200[/td]
    [/tr]
  [tr]
        [td]III[/td]
        [td]2-3[/td]
        [td]350-400[/td]
    [/tr]
  [tr]
        [td]IV[/td]
        [td]5-8[/td]
        [td]500+[/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[i]Some notes about resource uses:
[list]
[*] Cavalry needs Horses
[*] Better armour needs Steel
[*] High-end units may require other resources
[/list][/i]
These changes aim to provide a more nuanced and strategic combat experience with your feedback. Feel free to share your feedback on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1812910/discussions/]Steam forums[/url], we're eager to keep improving the game mechanics with you!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: February Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,
 
This month has been marked by a lot of invisible work for your eyes. First and foremost, we have been putting our shoulder to the wheel in the making of the [b]Civil War feature[/b]. We have made progress on designing how it will play out, the conditions and outcomes, as well as defining and creating the UI. This feature is dedicated to late game and asks for a lot of design work, hence the smaller updates recently. There's still much ahead of us, but we're headed in the right direction! Stay tuned for more information about it, the rule of every House will be challenged, and Calderia will be in flames!

Aside from the Civil War, we have been focusing on [b]improving existing features[/b], [b]UI[/b], fixing [b]bugs[/b] and [b]issues[/b], and also [b]finding ways to make the best of your feedback[/b]. You have shared a lot of valuable elements in your reviews and posts, we would like to [b]thank you[/b] for this. Now, without further ado, let’s get into the changes made this month!

[h2]Design & Balancing[/h2]

[b]Siege:[/b] We have been working on various improvements and balancing tweaks to the siege mechanics. You can now change your garrison units to adapt them to the attackers' troops, allowing you to make more tactical decisions. We added more clarity and details regarding the garrison with more tooltips and the garrison view UI. The AI now handles siege better, but in some cases, siege wasn't working properly when the AI didn't have a defending army. We have then added an event if a siege occurs without opposing forces. A few issues, like garrisons that wouldn't be removed after a conquest, have been fixed. Some siege events may still incorrectly refer to "Bandits" in their description or title, we are investigating it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/2b9e2ada24d2a8c68b3b80f43415db09f155a013.png[/img]

[b]War and fights:[/b] We reviewed and reflected on your feedback about the war and the mini-game for battles. We are working on improving the war system and adding a new military unit logic. While the battle system will [b]remain the same in its core[/b] (a mini-game with a board and units to control), we have been focusing on making it more entertaining and tactical. A fair share of the changes we have made are already available in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1812910/view/4138316032665459841][b]today’s regular update[/b][/url]. We will break the rework of the system down soon in the next devblog!
For more transparency, redesigning the battle system altogether would be heavily time- and resource-intensive, preventing us from working on other features and content for the game. We opted to make battles and social conflicts (negotiations) [b]totally skippable[/b] when we released the game in Early Access in August. You can simply select your units, as well as the objectives and outcomes you are most interested in, rather than going through the mini-games, if you do not want to play them.

[b]Winning path:[/b] We have fixed a bug that would softlock your progression in the Winning Condition Chapter VII “Building a Network of Power”, preventing you from finishing the game if you inadvertently completed steps in another order.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/b262f127d06718084a059a5458ca3c4a128bc5c3.png[/img]

[h2]Visuals & Interface[/h2]

[b]World map:[/b] We have noticed after reading your comments that there was information that was not clear enough or hard to find. Some of the information that has been mentioned can be viewed in the [b]map modes[/b]. Thanks to your input, it made us realize that the map modes we made for the world map a few months ago may have gone unnoticed. These modes [b]display important information[/b] by activating them and clicking on each territory to see, for instance, the [b]relations[/b] between Heads of House, and we added the possibility to view [b]unmarried characters[/b] using this map mode (how many there are in each fiefdom as well as their gender). It is also possible to view the [b]feudal status[/b] of each House (vassals and lieges), the [b]resources[/b], the recruited [b]spies[/b], the ongoing [b]wars[/b] (and who is at war with whom), and the [b]alliances[/b] of each House. We have added an [b]active map mode indicator[/b] for more clarity. We welcome your feedback to further improve this feature’s readability and clarity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/5f7ddef58a37be97d81e775a6caed2653eb04e74.png[/img]

[b]User Interface:[/b] Regarding the UI, we have added a fiefdom mouseover visual effects, tooltips breaking the production down to make it clearer, but also fixed a bug where it showed too many war reparations gains during wartime.

[b]User Interface scaling:[/b] In February, we kept working on the UI scaling issues and have set the default scale at 70%. This can be adjusted from the Video Settings. Please let us know if this improved the encountered issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/f6a38942734fe4835e678c644232b4072d44b8fe.png[/img]

[h2]Technical fixes & optimization[/h2]

[b]Optimization:[/b] We continued working on optimizing the game and especially the world map. We have added new options to the menu for visual effects and graphic settings, as well as Low and Medium graphic settings for charging water textures (rivers and lakes, in particular).

[b]Crash:[/b] We have fixed the reported crashes sent through the Unreal Engine Crash Report, in particular the one linked to loading a save. If you experience a crash, please send the crash report via the Unreal Engine Crash Report window, and let us know on Discord or in the Steam forums.

[h3]For more information, read the full aggregated patch notes below:[/h3]

[b]Added[/b]
[list]
[*] Siege info tooltips 
[*] Garrison view close button
[*] Event for Siege without opposing force
[*] Active map mode indicator
[*] Low and Medium graphic settings for water
[/list]
[b]Updated[/b]
[list]
[*] Rivers and lake textures
[*] Fiefdom mouseover visual effects
[*] Relation Map mode now shows unmarried court members
[*] Production breakdown tooltips
[*] World map optimizations
[/list]
[b]Fixed[/b]
[list]
[*] Remove unnecessary notification text on Trade and Raise Army views
[*] Resource breakdown can show too many war reparations gains
[*] Sue for Peace not triggered in some scenarios by AI
[*] Intrigue Back button not working
[*] Winning Condition Chapter VII rare softlock
[*] Siege not working properly when the enemy (AI) doesn’t have a defending army
[*] Incorrect confirmation texts
[*] Garrisons can’t be closed after conquest
[*] Various crash causes
[*] Game crash when loading a save
[/list]
[b]Known Issues[/b]
[list]
[*] Some siege events may incorrectly refer to "Bandits" in their text
[*] Default UI scale is at 70%, adjust this from Video Settings.
[*] UI scaling might cause some buttons to go outside the screen on some resolutions. To fix this, adjust the UI scaling percentage in Video Settings.
[*] Character customization images might fail to load occasionally. The UI still works, and reopening the menu sometimes fixes the issue.
[/list]
As you've seen, we've been keeping ourselves busy, and there's still much work to be done. We can't wait to hear your feedback on the Civil War! Keep watch for more updates on the development of Great Houses of Calderia and upcoming content!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: The art of negotiation
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

In today's devblog, we'll tackle [b]social conflicts[/b] and how they play a pivotal role in your nobles' lives. Social conflicts are common in Calderia and part and parcel of [b]diplomacy[/b]. Each House has its own interests and plans. They lead to [b]negotiations[/b] where your characters and companions' skills will help you choose the outcomes that are most advantageous to you.

[h3]Understanding social conflicts[/h3]

Unlike military battles, where victory might be more straightforward, social conflicts involve negotiation "fields" in the form of [b]boards[/b] where you place your character and companions. The board is made of [b]nodes[/b] and paths that represent [b]verbal sparring[/b] that you must win by conquering the nodes. When characters or companions meet, they argue until one of them backs away. You and AI alike can [b]prioritize specific topics[/b], making negotiations more intricate and goal-oriented. These conflicts can include trade, marriage, and peace negotiations, for instance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/ab3cf813930c6ae3c070d978ddd936b84e1b6b30.png[/img]

[h3]Impact of family members and companions[/h3]

[b]Family member characteristics and abilities[/b]
Each family member possesses [b]basic stats[/b] like "[b]attack[/b]" and [b]health[/b], influencing their strengths in negotiations. Additionally, [b]personality traits[/b] grant them extra abilities, some passive and others active. These abilities, ranging from automatic impacts to temporary boosts, significantly affect conflict dynamics and make your family member a determining part of the negotiation.

[b]Role of companions[/b]
Companions, representing the [b]household staf[/b]f, are useful assets in social conflicts. They are unlocked through [b]fiefdom upgrades[/b] and accompany family members in negotiations. When starting a negotiation, you will have to choose which ones will take part in the social conflict. Higher-tier companions possess stronger abilities, better health, and "attack" values. They are all [b]specialized[/b] in one of the four following skills: Diplomacy, Economy, Intrigue, or Military.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/6ff16752f7f4ff8d82e876ea4b947dec3eaa36ff.png[/img]

[h3]Dynamics and outcomes of social conflicts[/h3]

[b]Negotiation dynamics[/b]
During social conflicts, the selection of companions and their abilities influence negotiation outcomes. Companions may leave negotiations due to depleted health or nerves to [b]rest[/b], impacting the negotiation process. If they have [b]good composure[/b] (symbolized by the heart icons), then they [b]can return[/b] to the negotiations shortly after resting. However, if they are out of hearts, they cannot return to the board of the current conflict anymore.

[b]Long-term effects[/b]
Successfully managing social conflicts grants [b]various benefits[/b], including [b]traits[/b], [b]skills[/b], and [b]Tradition points[/b]. These outcomes make your House and characters more skilled for future negotiations. In summary, social conflicts are part of the diplomatic depth we wanted to develop. Choose the family members and companions you will use to solve them carefully so you can talk your way to the most profitable outcome.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/a0c7bd632af81a9c50320360c25b0086f8f5b008.png[/img]

And that concludes our devblog for today. Understanding the dynamics, stakes, abilities, and skills of social conflicts is part of your journey to become the most powerful House in Calderia!

Want to contribute to the game's improvement? You can do so by sharing your feedback and suggesting what you'd like to see in the game on our [url=https://discord.gg/m7xbmjHbK4]Discord[/url] or [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1812910/discussions/]Steam forums[/url]!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: January Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,
 
The beginning of the year was marked by many rounds of [b]polishing[/b] and [b]balancing[/b], especially with some [b]tweaks to the Bandits features[/b], but let’s not forget about the [b]addition of the Siege mechanics[/b]! We’ll dig deeper into this new content later in this Development Update. Thank you for your detailed feedback about the Bandits. With the information you shared, we have been able to make some adjustments to it. A lot of constructive input and e are also reviewing and discussing suggestions that you shared in the Steam discussions and reviews. As always, we deeply appreciate your involvement, and this is what fuels our creativity and minds to make the game even better, thanks to you!

[h2]Design & Balancing[/h2]

[b]Bandits and safety:[/b] As mentioned above, thanks to your input, we have been able to[b] balance the bandits' attacks[/b] on the map, especially in the [b]early phase of your fiefdom[/b]. This led to tweaks in many areas of this feature: bandits delegations now have more dynamic costs, more choices to make, and more varying outcomes, [b]bandits can no longer siege players repeatedly[/b], and the fiefdom starting safety is set to 2 instead of reverting to 0. In terms of UI, we have improved the safety tooltip and how it shows the thresholds for the next level, as well as the safety icon, which now shows its progression. Lastly, the AI bandit movement has been upgraded.

[b]Siege:[/b] The Siege feature is progressively implemented. This month, the feature is now playable with the elements we added: timers, information on the map, health loss for defenders over time, siege and garrison UI and UX. Buildings can impact siege duration and speed.
[b]How does it work?[/b] A Siege starts [b]when an army attacks an enemy city[/b]. When sieged, the defender must raise a [b]garrison[/b]. This is without the cost of raising an army for some of the units (although upkeep still must be paid). The attacking army starts building siege equipment, and when ready, it can attempt to assault the fiefdom. The progress of the siege equipment is shown on the siege tower icon. The [b]defending army loses health[/b] while under siege, and all [b]resources from production[/b] locations [b]and trade stop[/b] for the time being. The defender may try to lift the siege at any time. We've also updated how the armies work. When the army is raised, it does not automatically leave the city but is instead stationed in a garrison within the city.
 
[b]AI:[/b] Following the balance of the Bandits feature, the [b]AI now manages its safety production[/b] better to be [b]less likely to be attacked[/b] and overwhelmed by bandits. It also fights bandits back to protect its land. The way AI handles its production and storage has been improved as well.

[b]War and alliances:[/b] Regarding allies, we have applied a few changes. It is now not possible to declare war against an ally. On the other hand, you will [b]break an alliance by refusing to assist an ally[/b] at war if they ask for your support. In terms of UI, War and Alliance states are shown on the family crest. As for the war, army movement has improved. You have reported that army resources were not returned when an army was disbanded. It is now effective, and [b]disbanding an army partially returns the resources spent[/b] to raise it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/c440ff2ce2a67f261e9d6c89aa6889dfe62d7a30.png[/img]

[h2]Visuals & Interface[/h2]

[b]User Interface scaling:[/b] We are still experimenting with wide-screen resolutions. UI scaling is still a long, ongoing process, and we welcome feedback to help us optimize it during the whole Early Access phase. We have added a [b]master control to change all scalability settings[/b] at once in the Settings menu.
 
[b]Visuals alignment:[/b] We continued working on the text, button, and icon alignments to improve and harmonize the overall UI and interface menus.

[b]Visual FX and clarity:[/b] We have been working on adding a fair share of audiovisual feedback lately, like sound effects when declaring a war (on top of the change applied to the crest during a war), visual effects after a battle on the map, a bird particle system, showing ranks timeline progress, and growth indicator colors depending on the overall happiness level. You can change the visual effects quality in the Settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/2c739f6097561b91872788f4297b003d1dcc3dcb.png[/img]

[h2]Technical fixes & optimization[/h2]

[b]Optimization:[/b] We have been focusing on [b]optimizing the game[/b] in general, but only particularly on the world map, as it is the main screen. The [b]overall performance of the game has improved[/b] thanks to your input. We also focused on particle, day-cycle, and scalability settings optimization. This is still an ongoing process to improve the game on all kinds of setups and monitors. Please let us know if you encounter issues regarding the User Interface, the stability of the game, or other similar issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/3235a20b6efaab97a458cf473a2f5632bddf42ea.png[/img]

notes.title: December Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,
 
[b]Happy New Year[/b], and we hope you had a fantastic holiday! [b]We’re back at the office[/b], and it’s time to do a recap of what we did in December!

As you may have noticed, we are still [b]reworking[/b] the [b]UI[/b] and [b]AI[/b] on top of the [b]additional features coming progressively[/b]. [b]Bandits[/b] are [b]now here to disrupt your fiefdom[/b] and your rule! You can also [b]win the game by choosing a more diplomatic path[/b], thanks to the [b]Scholars and Schemers traditions[/b].
 
[b]Your contribution and extensive comments[/b] after the addition of the Bandits feature in December are [b]greatly appreciated[/b]! This is exactly why we chose Early Access—to be able to experiment and improve the game features with your help! As always, [b]thank you for your support and your commitment[/b], this is invaluable and crucial to the game process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/34b90c33f56f617d0918eb9f20597eeb69ca3575.png[/img]

[h3]Design & Balancing[/h3]

[b]Bandits[/b]: A major update has been made to the world map with the appearance of bandits on the roads. [b]No path is as safe as it used to be[/b] for merchants and soldiers. This feature comes with a [b]series of[/b] brand [b]new[/b] and [b]unique events[/b] you’ll have to deal with when they appear. While the feature is new to the game, [b]several iterations are required[/b] in the coming months [b]to balance it properly[/b], especially at the beginning of a new game. Thanks to all of you who have already spotted some issues with it and have suggested a few ideas to improve it.
 
[b]Traditions[/b]: New traditions have been implemented and tested, including the « [b]Dozen Peers[/b] » of the [b]Idealist path[/b] (which unlocks the Noble Advisor companions and units) and the « [b]Holy Knowledge[/b] » of the [b]Scholar path[/b] (which increases Scholar professions happiness from wages by +1 but doubles wage consumption).
 
[b]AI[/b]: With the new [b]Bandits[/b] feature, the [b]AI is now considering these attacks and[/b] unexpected [b]Bandits events[/b] in its plan. Its [b]overall plans[/b] have been [b]tweaked and improved[/b] as well.
 
[b]New winning condition[/b]: A [b]more diplomatic way[/b] of winning the game has been added thanks to the addition of the [b]Scholars and Schemers tradition perks[/b].

[b]Resources, costs, and buildings[/b]: [b]Production consumption[/b] has been [b]globally revisited[/b]. The [b]Cooperage building[/b] now has its [b]own category[/b] in the Fiefdom building menu, and bonus & penalty words for the refinement costs are now visible.

[b]Safety production[/b]: In connection with the [b]Bandits[/b] feature, the [b]safety of fiefdom production[/b] is now [b]more important[/b] than ever.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/a908c68bb44d96a3ccb2026d2bc8b2722f6ec6fe.png[/img]

[h3]Visuals & Interface[/h3]

[b]User Interface scaling[/b]: We are still experimenting with wide-screen resolutions. UI scaling is still a long, ongoing process and we welcome feedback to help us optimize it during the whole Early Access phase.
 
[b]Visuals alignment[/b]: Text, button and icon alignments have been reworked in some of the interface menus as well as in the event description to look better.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/b470b34eaa8c7acce5d30d5c46650a4d27aba6b9.png[/img]

[h3]Technical fixes & optimization[/h3]

[b]Crash fixes[/b]: [b]Loading a save file from an older version doesn’t cause the game to crash anymore[/b]. We also fixed a crash linked to a new tradition perk: « Holy Knowledge » when dragging workers into the scholar professions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/deb3685de663d3b86136c06a556f4c087f60d9bd.png[/img]

notes.title: House and character relations
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

Today, we would like to describe the [b]House and character relations system[/b] in more depth. [b]Everything[/b] in Calderia [b]revolves around relationships[/b], characters’ [b]reputations[/b] and [b]traits[/b]. Despite the stakes, it all comes down to [b]interpersonal connections[/b]. Your [b]deeds[/b] and your [b]personality are pivotal[/b] in events and in negotiations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/faf880dd462ddcc07eb7ce611111df86e5c09c0d.png[/img]

[h2]The role of Heads of House and personal relationships[/h2]

The [b]relationships between the Heads of Houses[/b], as leaders and representatives of their families, [b]are at the center of all House relations[/b]. The official stance between two families is shaped by the mutual liking of their leaders. [b]Your Head of House is the biggest influence[/b] on the way your House is perceived in Calderia. But that's just the tip of the iceberg. [b]Specific deeds[/b] by family members [b]can also add penalties or bonuses[/b], affecting how Houses view one another on an individual level. The [b]numeric values between Heads of House and individuals[/b] also have an [b]impact[/b] on many [b]actions[/b] and [b]decisions[/b] that you will take. Of course, the Head of House holds influence, but it's not the only character you get to play! [b]Each family member of your House is a playable character[/b], and [b]they have their own connections[/b] to all the other families.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/10e6bde93d61025943f46d21a898b6a68b085e0c.png[/img]

These [b]personal relationships between families[/b] can [b]spill over[/b], affecting all members. We decided to intertwine these relationships to add depth to the narrative, [b]making family ties a more impactful aspect of gameplay[/b]. Talking about [b]relationships[/b] inevitably leads to [b]alliances[/b], wars and conflicts in Calderia. [b]Alliances[/b] aren't arbitrary—they're [b]forged through marriage[/b]. It is a means to an end, more than a candid connection. Allies are useful assets to call upon in times of war.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/729d82987f6127bfcbf7be123b0bed62e2d4718a.png[/img]

[h2]Relationships based on personalities and reputations[/h2]

In most events, whether diplomatic or trade-focused, [b]relations between participants play a pivotal role[/b]. [b]House relations[/b], in addition to [b]personal relationships[/b], [b]can influence outcomes[/b]. Some actions, like declaring [b]war[/b], [b]require extremely negative House relations[/b]. Your Head of House must have bad relations with the Head of the House you want to start a war against. When it comes to [b]trade[/b], it isn't simply an economic activity in Calderia; it's a [b]diplomatic tool and lever[/b]. [b]Trading can improve or deteriorate relations[/b] between Houses. Fair deals foster goodwill, while exploiting others can strain relations. It's a nuanced system where every trade decision has consequences beyond material gains.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/6240eda1ef895d2aa7c2f877d57726c5adfc717b.png[/img]

[b]Relations with the Viceroy[/b] aren't just a formality or to be ignored—they [b]impact the selection order of the Ranks of Calderia[/b]. As the game progresses, [b]House relations with the Viceroy[/b] gain more and more meaning, [b]influencing your standings in the Civil War[/b], which we will add in the coming months.
[b]Character traits play a fundamental role[/b] in interacting with one another and developing relationships. From [b]personality[/b] and [b]mood[/b] to the character's [b]reputation[/b], these [b]traits establish basic relations between individuals[/b], even when meeting for the first time. The dynamic interactions based on the personalities and other traits of the characters contribute to the intricate connections that Houses and families form in Calderia.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/6158d2826361e0dd97d6720cf54e37992fba1b45.png[/img]

As demanding and complicated [b]relationships[/b] can be, they [b]cannot be overlooked[/b] when you are a noble seeking greater power and influence in Calderia.

This marks the end of this devblog on House and character relations. Want to contribute to the game's improvement? You can do so by sharing your feedback and suggesting what you'd like to see in the game on our [url=https://discord.gg/m7xbmjHbK4]Discord[/url] or [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1812910/discussions/]Steam forums[/url]!

- ❄️ Great Houses of Calderia Team 🎁 -

notes.title: New updated roadmap!
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

Game development is quite an adventure! We're really happy and thrilled by the thorough feedback and support we get, it helps us move forward and improve the game. Many of you requested [b]information on our roadmap[/b], and here we come with this [b]early Xmas present[/b]: our [b]new updated roadmap[/b]!

Because we are in Early Access and [b]game development is an organic process[/b], we've [b]made a few adjustments[/b] to our initial roadmap. We adapt to your input, and there are a few things that we decided to prioritize, like the "[b]Siege[/b]" feature, [b]reinforcing the family's traits[/b] and [b]traditions[/b], and [b]new winning paths[/b].

Since the game's Early Access release, [b]we've implemented new elements[/b] such as more [b]traditions[/b], [b]traits[/b], [b]character customization portraits[/b], conflict resolution adjustments, [b]AI improvement[/b], community suggestions, polish, and balancing based on your feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/196c2215a1a07fe307f6732a8e3ac45a371a5590.png[/img]

Throughout the development process, [b]your feedback is incredibly important to us[/b]. We value actively connecting with you and carefully assessing the ideas you share with us. We will still answer any questions you may have while working on adding more depth and content to the game.

[h2]Updated Roadmap[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/9cfb690dcfa801c4aa798a8bea3ab979398c1868.png[/img]

[b]New major features[/b] are coming very soon, like the "[b]Bandits[/b]", who will bring trouble with [b]incidents on the map[/b], affecting your trade delegations and causing diplomatic matters to be solved with other Houses. A [b]new winning path[/b] is on the way to let you win with a more [b]pacifist route[/b] (we know you love that too!). We still have [b]new traditions and family traits[/b] in store to reinforce the identity of your noble family and the impact of your choices. In the coming months, we're planning to add the [b]Civil War[/b], which, as you can expect, will disrupt the [b]seemingly peaceful land of Calderia[/b] and let the rivalry between Houses boil even more. It will add not only a [b]new winning path[/b] but also [b]more events related to Civil War[/b]. As for war (and not only the Civil War), we're adding the [b]Siege feature[/b] that you'll be able to implement in your strategy to subdue your enemies.
Many [b]rounds of balancing and polishing[/b] will be pushed, as we've continuously been doing so far. This also includes AI and other features.

We will keep on [b]sharing our progress and highlight the biggest additions and modifications[/b] in our [b]Monthly Development Update[/b] as we work towards the full release of Great Houses of Calderia.

Stay tuned for more updates as we strive to craft the best version possible of our take on the grand strategy genre. We want to [b]thank you[/b], your support fills us with determination, and we are confident that we can succeed with your help.

- ❄️ Great Houses of Calderia Team 🎁 -

notes.title: November Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,
 
This month has been quieter, but for a good reason! The team gathered to [b]review[/b] and [b]rework[/b] on a deeper level [b]several aspects of the game[/b], like the [b]AI and UI[/b], but also [b]add more depth to the family legacy[/b] based on Traditions and traits. This is a long and complicated process, but we believe that it is for the better. Our objective is to make Calderia more and more vivid and dynamic.
 
We thank you for your support and your contribution to the discussions, which allow us to improve the game based on your feedback.

[h3]Design & Balancing[/h3]

[b]Family traits[/b]: With the family traits comes their inheritance. There is a small chance to receive traits from the parents at birth. They are meant to strengthen the family identity and influence their behavior based on Traditions, choices and event outcomes.
 
[b]Traditions[/b]: New traditions have been implemented and tested, including the « Calderian Mysteries » of the Schemers path (which can influence Viceroy's relations against the House of any Duke or Count) and the « Celebrating Life » of the Peacemakers path (every summer season worker's crop consumption is doubled, but every worker's happiness gets +1).
 
[b]AI[/b]: November marks a milestone in the AI’s rework, especially in short and long-term fiefdom management. We have been improving AI’s plans to take action on many elements: war, fiefdom management, and resource production. Trade is left untouched for now, but it will be tackled in the coming weeks. The point of this deep rework is to make you feel like Calderia is vivid and dynamic.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/048ff189168b48371423c848eb0545d35bc67b81.png[/img]

[h3]Visuals & Interface[/h3]

[b]User Interface scaling[/b]: This month, the team has led research and experiments for wide screen resolution. UI scaling is still a long, ongoing process and we welcome feedback to help us optimize it during the whole Early Access phase.
 
[b]Tutorial[/b]: We’ve also added new steps to the tutorial for features such as the Intrigue and Trade. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/428637b4a169ecc17ca47df68c6096037a0cffb8.png[/img]

notes.title: October Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

We can't thank you enough for your active role in Great Houses of Calderia. Your [b]participation in discussions[/b] and [b]feedback sharing[/b] had a [b]significant impact on[/b] the [b]game's development[/b]. This summary shines a light on the [b]changes[/b], [b]improvements[/b], and [b]system adjustments[/b] that have been made, all [b]thanks to your invaluable input[/b]. We're excited to keep shaping the game with your feedback. Enjoy!

[h3]Design & Balancing[/h3]

[b]Game ending and further:[/b] As requested, we added the possibility to pursue your rule even after the end of the game, whether you completed the objectives of “Road to Victory” or not.

[b]Ranks:[/b] The Ranks of Calderia feature wasn’t working as intended. It has been reworked and improved, it should now be working as designed. Rank appeal social conflicts no longer provide skill increases to avoid save-load scumming to rapidly grind skills.

[b]Conflict Resolution:[/b] We added more outcomes to the social conflicts to make them more impactful and meaningful. Failing or winning a conflict now has consequences for each character.

[b]AI:[/b] This month allowed us to iterate and rework the AI in several aspects. We improved its behavior and plans for long-term play. This is part of our ongoing balancing and one of our main focus points during the whole Early Access phase.

[b]War:[/b] Warscore has been revisited, as has army behavior on the map. The work on AI has an impact on war. It does more checks before considering starting a war or taking a decision during a war. This includes assessing the strength of its enemies and adapting to the course of the war. Regarding UI, there are new war icons for the Fiefdom Widget, making it easier to know what is happening in the game. If you click on a Crest icon during a war, the camera will focus on the Fiefdom related to it.

[b]Traditions:[/b] A set of new Traditions has been added to expand the Tradition tree. You can choose from a larger set of perks to customize your family and rule. On top of this, the AI and its behavior are now more influenced by its Tradition.

[b]Events[/b]: There was a problem with the Marriage Action Prompt, but it has been fixed now. We added new event text and added results to make it more diverse. Building "Schools of Wisdom" in other fiefdoms now provides better events connected to them. When appealing for a higher rank or dealing with trade events, you will sometimes face social conflicts, if you successfully solve them, you can get free spies as a reward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/b3669818efebd9ab7980e603a2a863252639708a.png[/img]

[h3]Visuals & Interface[/h3]

[b]Character customization:[/b] In September, we added the Character customization feature. More portrait pieces have now been added so that you can customize your characters even more! We also added more tooltips regarding this feature.
