notes.title: Military: The art of war and feudalism
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

Today, we delve into the [b]intricate art of war[/b], linked with diplomacy and economy, in Great Houses of Calderia. [b]War is motivated by the influence of feudal politics and the pursuit of nobility ranks in Calderia[/b]. Let's explore the key features of how war works.

There are [b]specific steps and thresholds to meet the conditions for wars[/b] to be declared, they are shown at the war tooltip in military delegation view. You must have negative relations with the House you want to attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/7225dd7c969e210c780a1fa3dcf8490eb9a98671.png[/img]

[b]Here are the current war types and their requirements:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Humiliation war[/b]: You must have House relations lower than -40. Winning this war allows you to either have a claim on their title or vassalize them.
[*] [b]Vassalization war[/b]: You must have House relations lower than -60, have the right to vassalize and have a higher rank than the opposing House. Winning this war allows you to vassalize this House, which will then pledge allegiance and pay taxes to you.
[*] [b]Title war[/b]: You must have House relations lower than -85, have the right to claim the title of the opposing House. Winning this war grants you the title of the defeated House, which will then go down to your previous title. For instance, you had the Baron rank before winning the Title War. The House you attacked had the Count rank, you then become a Count and they become a Baron.
[*] [b]Tax war[/b]: This war can only be declared to vassals who are refusing to pay taxes they owe you. Winning this war will resume the tax payments the House owes you.
[/list]


[h3]Units and warfare[/h3]
Developing your fiefdom and [b]making new buildings allows you to unlock new military units[/b], each with its own unique strengths and roles on the battlefield. Units come with both a [b]raise cost[/b] and an [b]upkeep cost[/b], requiring you to balance your military might with your resources. All units have attack, defense, health and attack speed variables. Some units can have special abilities that may be automatic, like ranged abilities, while others need to be activated. [b]Defense reduces attack damage input and the attacker also takes some damage[/b]. [b]Military units[/b], once engaged, [b]are caught up in the battle[/b] and [b]require time to retreat[/b] before they can escape the fight. This adds dynamics to the ebb and flow of battles. [b]Wounded units who[/b] managed to [b]retreat[/b] in time [b]join the reserve[/b], where [b]they can slowly heal[/b] so you can redeploy them again. On the other hand, units who died during the fight cannot be used again for future battles during the ongoing war. With this game mechanic, we wanted to encourage a thoughtful rotation of troops to optimize your strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/a096d3060ee8ca75082c25f4afad14d51365dd27.png[/img]

[h3]Rising in the nobility ranks[/h3]
You must first successfully [b]make a claim to a higher title[/b] to advance in nobility. [b]Wars are an effective way to rise in the nobility ranks[/b]. They allow you to take over the title of the House ruling over you. But first, you must declare and win a [b]Humiliation War[/b], [b]then a Title War to obtain a new title[/b]. You can progress through nobility ranks one level at a time, from Baron to Count, Count to Duke, and from Duke to Viceroy. [b]Marriage is a powerful asset for forging alliances[/b] between the families tied by the union. These [b]allies can then be called to join wars[/b], strengthening your military power. Growing your influence and military power starts at the court, the relationships you build are essential to your success.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/36ade319ce536ad7e16eba5d3666b21ee9b800c2.png[/img]

[h3]Peace negotiations and war weariness[/h3]
Wars cannot last forever. [b]Every war concludes with peace negotiations[/b]. The possible [b]outcomes[/b] are [b]determined by various elements based on how the war ended[/b]. It affects the terms that you can focus on during negotiations. However, [b]total wins and total losses have automatic outcomes[/b]. Engaging in war leads to [b]war weariness[/b] that accumulates at varying levels, [b]each with its own cumulative impacts[/b]. Successive wars also increase your war weariness. War weariness takes time to wear off during peace, and [b]peace treaties come with a truce period[/b] that prevents new wars from being declared right after a war ends. [b]Winning a war grants you an advantage in peace negotiations[/b], as the losing party will have fewer companions to bargain with. Be aware that refusing ally calls to aid them in war degrades your reputation and strains relations with all the other Houses. You have to balance your own interests with your reputation and relations with other Houses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/2b7dc0fe99673d396f8b8304e9d7e809b7193e6e.png[/img]

[h3]Resource management and war impact[/h3]
Because [b]resources[/b] like crops, livestock, materials, metal ore, horses, and grapes [b]are produced outside the city[/b], they are easy targets during war. [b]Blockades on roads[/b] to the city from resource locations [b]disrupt the resource supply chain[/b] and prevent the fiefdom from receiving the resources. On top of the blockades that can affect your resources and economic sustainability, [b]enemy armies can burn down your production buildings[/b] that won’t produce resources until they are repaired. [b]Defending and repairing your production buildings is crucial[/b] to maintaining your ability to upkeep your armies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/1f7836ed46bd8456ed4928df2f96a7621ccb51a5.png[/img]

[h3]Siege and warscore[/h3]
[b]Losing a battle[/b] will have the remains of the army [b]retreat automatically[/b] on the map for a while, [b]giving a head start for the pursuing army[/b]. For now, [b]siege has a static time period during which walls can be broken[/b]. [b]Conquering a castle grants[/b] a significant amount of [b]points in the warscore[/b], and [b]maintaining a siege[/b] also [b]accumulates additional points over time[/b], which greatly contribute to victory. [b]All wars can end in five ways[/b], from [b]neutral peace to total victory or defeat[/b], allowing for varied approaches depending on the most interesting outcomes for you. Reaching [b]neutral peace negotiations will result in both Houses seeking to earn something from the deal[/b]. Battlefields provide temporary effects for battles. The [b]warscore[/b] to aim for [b]depends on the war type[/b]. Your tactical decisions should favor short and effective war resolutions rather than lengthy military conflicts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/a2804c9fbdda1607b75bc384a2b0cf8ec0e3c342.png[/img]

Now that we have tackled these features, giving you a better look at the way war works in the game, may you increase your chances of success and prevail with this knowledge. The complex art of military strategy, diplomatic and economic acuteness will shape the fate of your fiefdom.

May your banners fly high and your influence leave a lasting mark in the tapestry of power as you rise in the ranks of Calderia!

Join our [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord[/url] and share your feedback with us!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: September Development update
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

Once again, thank you for playing Great Houses of Calderia, participating in the discussions, sharing your feedback and helping us make the best game possible. This [b]summary highlights the changes, additions, and improvements made thanks to you[/b], as well as [b]significant adjustments to systems to balance the game[/b]. We did our best to meet your needs and make your experience more enjoyable! And as some of you might have noticed, [b]we added some news features in advance for you[/b]! Enjoy!

[h3]Design & Balancing[/h3]

[b]Extended game ending:[/b] Until the latest patch, becoming a Duke was the highest rank attainable at the time. With the recent patch, ending the game is now possible with either one of the two alternative outcomes: losing in 50 years if you fail to earn Viceroy rank or winning if you succeed in achieving Viceroy rank.

[b]Events:[/b] A better distribution of event spawn has been made as well to offer more variations. Also, events now have a seed ID that prevents them from spawning twice in a row or re-spawning exactly the same way if the player reloads a game before an event appears. Additional events have been added. We’ve corrected the outcomes of some events.

[b]Traditions:[/b] We added new nodes to the Tradition Tree: Bread and Circus (Idealists) and Light Mathemagic (Scholars). The Tradition you choose when you create your House now has more impact, it grants you 75% of the required points to access the first node. We also improved the clarity of the events linked to Traditions. We deactivated a Tradition node that would soft-lock the progression (Pacifist) until the diplomatic path becomes available. Additional traditions have been added to the Traditions tree.

[b]Fiefdom management:[/b] Building requirements have been rebalanced (cost to build and resource production), as well as the Happiness calculation system. More tooltips have been added. Companions unlock and production bonuses are rebalanced.

[b]Conflict Resolution:[/b] Additional tooltips have been added to units’ skills, playground effects. One new military unit and two new companions were added. Cooldown indication for units' abilities has been added. We fixed bugs that prevented dismissing your armies and pillaging buildings.

[b]Weddings & births:[/b] Chance of birth among married couples has increased (roughly x3 more often) in addition to rebalancing the statistics required to do weddings.

[b]Ranks:[/b] A few bugs preventing some Rank Effects from being triggered have been fixed. Clearer information is now provided in the titles' descriptions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/76dd5884e1a886613119c1f76642351592cd4783.png[/img]

[h3]Visuals & Interface[/h3]

[b]Character portrait customization:[/b] You can now customize the portraits of any of your family members! Click on “i” on your character, then click on the quill icon to edit your character. You can rearrange the appearance with a set of various head shapes, hairstyles, clothing and armour.

[b]User Interface scaling:[/b] To cover a wider range of resolutions, we’ve reworked the interfaces of the game to allow for more scalability on wider and smaller resolutions. We’ll regularly continue working on it to improve it the best we can. We’ll run more tests on different settings in the future to make sure we cover the most standard ones.

[b]Readability:[/b] Conflict action menu, Trade meter display and Ranks of Calderia layout have been reworked for better readability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/05e009a49d9ad3bcb737655ff9f33f4757972363.png[/img]

[h3]Technical fixes & optimization[/h3]
 
[b]Crash fixes:[/b] Regarding the crashes, please consider sending the crash report using the Unreal Crash Report panel. Doing so really helps us work on the causes of the crash and improve the game’s stability. This is one of our priorities and thanks to these crash reports, we have been able to fix the reported crashes.

[b]Memory leaks:[/b] Thanks to your input, we worked on the memory leaks that were due to background calculations during the long playthrough. We have managed to solve and optimize them. This issue should not occur anymore. Please let us know if you encounter any memory leaks so we can investigate them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/7879a2f13a7224ef7f57f5df1d965e9aace10823.png[/img]

notes.title: Making the fashion of Calderia
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

This is the beginning of Fashion Week in Paris! To celebrate this opportunity, we wanted to give you an [b]insight into our process behind making the fashion and clothing[/b] for Calderia.

The world of Calderia is a [b]mix of history and fantasy[/b]. We drew inspiration from the [b]Late Medieval to Early Renaissance periods[/b], focusing on [b]Mediterranean cultures[/b]. This was the starting point for the inspiration research. Calderia is a society built on gender equality, ancient mythology, Renaissance technology, and living on rough but rich soil where danger is constant. We wanted to highlight and create a tapestry of style that is both unique and meaningful to the setting. The process of making the fashion of Calderia is very similar to the steps of actual fashion design.

[h3]Setting and early research[/h3]
To bring this world to life, we undertook [b]extensive research[/b]. We immersed ourselves in the historical era, studying everything from clothing to architecture, art, and culture. This diligent research allowed us to develop an intuitive understanding of the era, which would later help us in our creative choices. Moreover, we [b]explored not only real-world historical sources but also drew inspiration from other fantasy realms[/b] set in similar time periods. Games like Warhammer Fantasy, The Witcher, and Dungeons & Dragons served as valuable references, but [b]we still aimed to find our own touch[/b].

[i]An illustration showing the mix between Ancient history and Renaissance.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/914e6e420896685f9a208bd1835cfb3b5176725d.jpg[/img]

[h3]Intuitive sketching and exploration[/h3]
One of the key creative processes in fashion design for Calderia involved [b]intuitive sketching[/b]. We aimed to produce as many drawings as possible without imposing strict limitations. This freedom to explore different styles and directions allowed us to [b]establish the essence of Calderian fashion[/b]. It was essential to explore the wrong paths as well, as this enabled us to better understand the surrounding styles and ultimately led to the one that felt right to us.

[i]Examples of approved sketches with interesting mood and style.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/ea20197d7fc595932e9a4cfec6a8b5bf9c3a6c10.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/f7ec6503a557a28a617046e4ba3eb7322770777c.png[/img]

[i]Examples of disapproved sketches which didn't fit our vision.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/d32337dff23b8e0676c073dbb3d7771bac4846ca.png[/img]

[h3]Chosen art direction: Italian and Spanish Renaissance[/h3]
After extensive research and exploration, we settled on a [b]fashion direction that drew heavily from Italian and Spanish influences[/b]. Our focus spanned from the [b]Late Medieval to the Early Renaissance, with hints of the High and Late Renaissance, particularly in Italy[/b]. We deliberately avoided the more commonly portrayed British, French, Burgundian, and German styles, seeking to establish a unique identity for Calderian fashion. [b]Armour pieces integrated with court dresses became a prominent feature[/b], signifying the noble status of characters in the game. This deviated from historical accuracy, as in Renaissance Italy, wearing armour was considered dangerous, as one would be then likely "looking for problems". However, it was a deliberate choice to emphasize the Calderians' interest in armours, and how they could be used to [b]show off the quality of craftsmanship and the wealth of their fiefdoms[/b].

[i]An illustration showing nobles walking in the city in a Mediterranean-inspired setting.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/ca7aca0119814cba66be4724f537877c56c8f674.jpg[/img]

[h3]Blending History and fantasy[/h3]
[b]Finding a balance between low fantasy and history posed an interesting challenge for us[/b]. We strived to explore historical components and take them slightly further towards fantasy. Elements such as gorgets and bevors, elaborate hairstyles, the extravagant use of pearls, and unique hats all contributed to the fantastical aspect of Calderian fashion. [b]The game's roots in ancient mythology are reflected in religious attire and ceremonies, blending with modern Renaissance garments[/b]. This fusion adds depth to the world, contributing to building the history and culture of Calderia based on a [b]unique tapestry woven from various sources of inspiration[/b].

[i]Examples of portraits mixing fantasy and real-life inspired clothing.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/60df74543ee585797842d2ee92aefc35a29d0256.png[/img]

[h3]Imperial distinction[/h3]
The [b]presence of the Imperial overlords is rare[/b] in Calderia, but when it does happen, it is unmistakable. Their [b]style is a blend of Medieval and High Renaissance influences, leaning toward the British, French, and Burgundy styles[/b] that are consciously avoided in Calderian fashion. Layering of opulent fabrics, the use of fur and leather, and a penchant for gloves all serve to distinguish the Imperial elite and show their wealth.

[i]Examples of research for imperial clothing.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/5629e83ee620a48c0ded315039e506e7502f4c8e.png[/img]

Calderian fashion is a [b]visual exploration of History and fantasy[/b], a uchronia that nurtures our creativity. You can find more information about the art of Calderia in our art book.

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: Revealing our 2023 Roadmap!
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

[h3]Great Houses of Calderia recently launched, we decided to reveal the roadmap![/h3]
We sincerely appreciate all of the positive feedback we've received from both players and the press! We'd also like to thank everyone for their thorough input as we work on enhancing the game. This is exactly what we are looking to make the best game possible with your contribution!

[h3]Roadmap[/h3]
The days, dare I say, years in the game are passing by. Your characters grow wiser, or dumber, and their leadership is constantly disrupted by the other Houses as you try to rise in the ranks of Calderia. It's time to share the plans for the next few months! We are continuously working on new features for you to try out and bug fixes. [b]Find out all we have planned for the first phase of Early Access in 2023[/b] in this much anticipated [b]roadmap[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/4202b321c74736eadf281836c59c8a91bcfba89c.png[/img]

The roadmap promises a number of major features, including [b]new Traditions[/b], the [b]updrade of the modding tool[/b]. With each update, there will be overall improvements, such as the addition of small features, the Quality of Life changes, and bug fixes.

[b]We welcome and value community feedback[/b], feel free to share your honest thoughts on the game. Because we are in Early Access and unexpected events may effect the game's development, the features on the roadmap may be subject to change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/a5114929fb0ee104926b5e0c82734a7c8873bdab.png[/img]
[i]Traditions tree[/i]

The [b]new traditions[/b] and [b]balancing[/b] are our priority, as they are [b]scheduled for this Q3[/b] as well as improvement on the modding tool. Following that, numerous major additions, including [b]new intrigue actions[/b], [b]character portrait customization[/b], [b]incidents happening on the map[/b] and along [b]community created events[/b] are [b]planned for Q4[/b]. We want to work hand-in-hand with our community to make the best game possible, so we are open to community suggestions!

Thank you for making this journey with us. We are excited by the idea of showing you everything else we've got in store for you.

[h3]Bug reports & feedback[/h3]
As a reminder, please share any bug reports and your feedback, ideas and suggestions in the Steam Discussions or via our [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord[/url].


- Great Houses of Calderia -

notes.title: 5 Tips to Start in Great Houses of Calderia
notes.content:
Great Houses of Calderia is now in [b]Early Access[/b] [b]on Steam[/b]. It is time to begin your training so that you become a worthy ruler in this [b]Feudal Grand Strategy[/b] game. Set in a world inspired by the Mediterranean Renaissance, the game invites you to step into the shoes of a Noble Family vying for dominance in the power-hungry province of Calderia.

As you embark on this strategic journey, here are five essential tips to guide you in your quest for power, influence, and victory.

[h3]Summary[/h3]
[b]Tip #1[/b] Know Your Characters Like the Back of Your Hand
[b]Tip #2[/b] Balance Diplomacy, Strategy, and Economy
[b]Tip #3[/b] Embrace Real-time Tactical Battles
[b]Tip #4[/b] Shape Your Family's Legacy
[b]Tip #5[/b] How to acquire new Agents & Units

[h2]1. Know Your Characters Like the Back of Your Hand:[/h2]
In Calderia, you aren't just a ruler; you're a leader managing an entire family. Each family member has a unique personality, traits, and desires. Take the time to understand their strengths and weaknesses, and assign them to roles that best suit their abilities. Keep in mind that characters' personalities can evolve, shaped by the events they experience.
Lastly, pick the right family member to manage your fiefdom's key operations to bolster your production and maintain the people´s happiness high!
Effective management of your family members is key to your success.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/5926c1c756d702156d53f0bcbb1f3b7db788ceaa.png[/img]

[h2]2. Balance Diplomacy, Strategy, and Economy:[/h2]
Calderia isn't just about battles on the field; it's a realm where wise schemes, thriving economies, and diplomatic prowess are just as crucial. Utilize a delicate balance of diplomacy, intrigue, and trade to expand your influence. Make critical decisions during diplomatic events and battles alike, as these moments can shape the tide of power in your favour.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/c0570b63d7f2ec714ea7f9771dbb23d965dc013c.png[/img]

[h2]3. Embrace Real-time Tactical Battles:[/h2]
When it comes to securing victory, battles are inevitable. Engage in real-time tactical battles that require careful planning and execution. Manage your units effectively on the battlefield to outmanoeuvre your opponents and claim victory. Remember, however, that battles are just one aspect of securing new titles and ascending the ranks of Calderia's hierarchy.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/ddd208b3e17721851b0e37c3eecac3d1254cb453.png[/img]

[h2]4. Shape Your Family's Legacy:[/h2]
Define the traditions, values, and goals of your family. These elements are the foundation of your legacy and the story you'll weave throughout the game. As you progress, you will experience the personal stories of your extended family, seeing your reputation grow and your influence expand. With the modding tool provided, you can even create unique, captivating narratives that further enrich the world of Calderia.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/76dd5884e1a886613119c1f76642351592cd4783.png[/img]

[h2]5. How to acquire new Agents & Units:[/h2]
The pool of Agents & Units is linked to the infrastructure.
Upgrading your region will not only increase your maximum Population and boost your production but also give you access to unique Agents that can help you in social conflicts or new Unit Types that can be recruited during wartime.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/737e1fccf04cb331a325f98f4cf1dbbb635af1e0.png[/img]

In conclusion, Great Houses of Calderia offers you an immersive experience in the complex world of Feudal Grand Strategy. By understanding your characters, mastering the art of diplomacy and strategy, embracing tactical battles, shaping your family's legacy, and adapting to the ever-changing landscape, you can rise from a fledgling noble family to seize the throne and achieve the ultimate goal of becoming the power-hungry Viceroy of Calderia. Good luck on your journey to dominion!

[previewyoutube=jrwe2qTxMnU;full][/previewyoutube]

- Great Houses of Calderia team -

notes.title: Early Access out NOW!
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

[h3]Great Houses of Calderia is launching [b]on Steam in Early Access now[/b] at a [b]20% discount[/b].[/h3]

Your strategic prowess will be your strongest asset as you navigate the unspoken hunger for power and influence in Calderia. Overthrow the ambitions and schemes of rival Houses as you expand your influence. Rise in the ranks of Calderia and become an even more powerful family.

The game is available in [b]English[/b] during Early Access.

Achieve your goal in this Feudal Grand Strategy by choosing various paths: diplomacy, intrigue, war, and economy. Manage your fiefdom, produce resources and assign tasks to your characters. Make allies, enemies, trade, arrange marriages, and appeal for the most useful rank to achieve objectives. Unveil the ancient history of the fantastic land of Calderia, its myths and its forgotten civilization.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/5efd559f8c3a3d89bd3641839e053d2fa911d09f.png[/img]

Your characters have their own personalities, constantly shaped by the events they will encounter, impacting their willingness and ability to serve you right. They have their own agenda and can escape your control to go on character journeys that will forever change them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/2a42a6481f22adb0f22538f40b970214aac16313.png[/img]

Hours of gameplay await you as you create your House and noble family. Participate actively in shaping the world of your characters by creating their coat of arms, choosing their traditions and values, their territory, and their storylines. There are numerous approaches to completing the game and hundreds of ways to play: unlock and discover traditions, noble ranks, and character traits.

[previewyoutube=nhAamg-gqAk;full][trailer][/previewyoutube]

[b]Choices matter[/b] – You will have to make difficult decisions to resolve a variety of situations, ranging from negotiating with other Houses to going to war. You must consider the advantages and disadvantages of each choice.

[b]Creating stories[/b] – Every decision you make in the game results in different outcomes and stories, whether they are related to diplomacy, war, or other events.

[b]Balancing Diplomacy and War[/b] – Both sides are equally important, and you need to engage actively in order to grow your influence. Manage battles, trading and diplomatic events with our conflict resolution system for battles on a real-time tactical resource management system.

[b]Impactful decisions[/b] – Everything you do in the game has a clear and visible effect. For example, if you dispatch a trading caravan, you will be able to observe and interact with the characters as they travel from your fiefdom to their destination.

[b]Easy to play[/b] – The game starts simple and becomes more complex as you progress in your quest for power.

Be wary of who you place your trust in, as “blood is thicker than water” stands as true as ever. The destiny of the family lies in its members’ hands alone. Explore the intricacies of the politics of this Mediterranean Renaissance-inspired world. The community's feedback during Early Access will help us improve and upgrade the existing features and any planned additions to the final release version.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/9f41dd741707f2a493edbc7d3d415940ff4a86bb.png[/img]

Experience unique events with our modding tool, allowing you to shape new stories. Your contribution will play an important role in the development and expansion of this tool to further customize the game, everything lies in your hands!

notes.title: What is Great Houses of Calderia?
notes.content:
Oy rulers!

Great Houses of Calderia is a [b]Feudal Grand Strategy game[/b], but, what is this? You play as a noble House trying to make your way to the most influential and powerful families of Calderia. You can achieve that goal by taking various paths: [b]diplomacy[/b], [b]intrigue[/b], [b]war[/b] and [b]economy[/b]. You also manage your territory on a small scale, the day-to-day aspects of your fiefdom and assign tasks to your characters as well as develop the relations with the other Houses of Calderia. Make allies, enemies, trade, arrange marriages, appeal for the most useful rank to complete your objectives.

[b]On August 30 in Early Access on Steam, build your family's legacy of power and rise in the ranks of Calderia.[/b]

[h2]Feudal Grand Strategy[/h2]
Great Houses of Calderia is a [b]political[/b] and [b]feudal simulation[/b] based on medieval European practices, focusing on land ownership, territorial administration and service-based relationships of power. It follows the vassal political system: Houses promise loyalty to higher authorities and answer directly to the Emperor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/f02ad01b69cf7cf820f54124f4ca7cba46848eac.jpg[/img]

[h3]1. Warfare[/h3]
You can be at war with other Houses to weaken them or make them your vassals. But wars are expensive and slow your fiefdom growth, so you should declare war very wisely and prefer short term conflicts over lasting civil wars. Raise your army and choose your units carefully, command them on the map and in conflict resolution. You overview conflicts and battles on a strategic scale. You resolve battles through tactical choices and the management of your army. Your control over the military units is through production, army movement and large scale battles.

[h3]2. Economy and Resource Management[/h3]
Resource management allows you to grow your fiefdom in many ways: allocating resources to fund wars, trading, and managing your stock. Resources are also used to pay your workers, make them happy and more efficient. You need to establish commercial relations if you want your economy to flourish and grow faster. Military units cost money to rally and upkeep, as do bribes if you want to take another route. Even if you choose war over diplomacy, peace negotiations are inevitable if you do not wish to be in debt.

[h3]3. House Relations and Diplomacy[/h3]
House relations are crucial for the progress of your fiefdom. You can declare war, make peace, form alliances, collect taxes, have vassals, embargo enemies, or request assistance against common foes. The game adds a management layer on a smaller scale to your fiefdom and family members, assigning them tasks like resource production, developing relations, and making official visits. Children take part in the scheme too, assign them to be wards and squires. You manage your House over multiple generations and as nobles, their lives are busy and rythmed by events; allowing them to learn, improve skills, and earn temporary traits.

[h3]4. Intrigues and schemes[/h3]
If diplomacy and war do not allow you to complete your goals, you can bring turmoil from the inside. Recruit spies and disrupt the rival’s fiefdom from within by various means. Spread propaganda, lead slander campaigns, set obstacles in their growth by hampering resource production, plan sly attacks on trading caravans, arson buildings and more. Outsmart the plans of your enemies and steal the power from them. This is a more cunning, deceiving and dishonest approach, but an effective one nonetheless.

[h3]Made by passionate indies[/h3]
Resistance Games is a Finnish indie game studio specializing in PC and console strategy games. Founded out of a passion for this genre and a desire to connect with players, we aim to create unique experiences through collaboration with our community. Great Houses of Calderia is developed by a small team of indie developers wishing to offer a unique perspective on this genre, blending familiar elements with innovative ideas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/c3aaa1cef495e1268cfe5e6a2b0d24d391e65b6a.jpg[/img]

[h2]A fresh take on the genre[/h2]

[h3]Diplomacy, war, intrigue and economy[/h3]
Opportunities can arise from both victory & defeat. War and diplomacy matter equally. Diplomatic events cover big social events and traditions like weddings and jousts. Engage in courtly life, trade, negotiations, and even spying on your neighbors. Make crucial choices during battles and important diplomatic events to get an edge over your enemies. Assign your most capable family members to lead delegations and interact with other Houses. Use each family member's abilities, both innate and learned, to achieve your goals.

[h3]Conflict resolution system[/h3]
In battles and important talks with other Houses, you need to make critical choices. These choices can give you advantages over your rivals. You handle battles using the Real-time tactical unit management system. But earning new titles isn't just about fighting – it's about being good at diplomacy, making deals, tricky plans, and successful trading. You get to be actively involved in controlling the course of important events, like dealing with other Houses or fighting in wars, by using our real-time tactical resource management system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/2f2ceb7eeb27846a0dcba954329888a6517166b5.png[/img]

[h3]Multiple paths to victory[/h3]
Make a lasting and powerful House in Calderia:
[list]
[*] Manage and expand your own fiefdom and its population.
[*] Become a higher member of the nobility and bring other Houses under your rule.
[*] Establish a rich tapestry of unique traditions for your House.
[*] Obtain honorary ranks that will play a major part in how your rule influences the fate of Calderia in the end.
[/list]
[h3]Community creation and modding[/h3]
Create and experience unique, captivating events within the game with our modding tool. Unleash your creativity and shape new narratives! Make your voice count, you can contribute to the development of the game with your feedback. We hope to make the best game possible with our community and the modding tool available for the Early Access release. Your contribution will play a big part in the development and expansion of this tool so you may further customize the game, everything lies in your hands!

[h3]Innovative elements[/h3]
Great Houses of Calderia combines fresh ideas to set itself apart as a creative and unique game:
[list]
[*] A conflict resolution system for battles and diplomatic events based on a real-time tactical resource management system
[*] Its artistic direction based on the Mediterranean Renaissance, bringing to the genre sunny and vibrant colors
[*] Fantasy setting rather than historical
[*] Key characters with their own agendas
[/list]
Play an active role in shaping your characters' world, designing the coat of arms of your House, choosing their traditions and values, their territory and the characters' storylines. There are multiple endings and hundreds of ways to play: unlock and discover traditions, noble ranks, and character traits by playing through the game in different ways.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/5b13563f39796a84019509322a1f9998f5857cf4.png[/img]

[b]Choices matter –[/b] You will need to make tough choices that resolve a wide range of situations, from negciating with other Houses to going to war. You will have to think about the good and bad sides of each choice.

[b]Creating stories –[/b] Every action you take in the game leads to various outcomes and stories, whether it's about diplomacy, war or other events.

[b]Balancing Diplomacy and War –[/b] Both aspects are equally important, and you need to take an active part to develop your influence.

[b]Impactful decisions –[/b] Everything you do in the game has a clear effect that you can see. For example, if you send a trading caravan, you will actually see and interact with the moving characters from your fiefdom to its destination.

[b]Easy to play –[/b] The game starts simple and progressively becomes more complex as you advance in your quest for power.


[h2]The world of Calderia[/h2]

[h3]Renaissance setting[/h3]
Calderia is a Mediterranean Renaissance-inspired land and earns its name from its most notable landmark, an old volcano with a warm-water lake in its caldera. Known as both the Old and New World, it was once home to a thriving civilization. However, a devastating disaster led to the inhabitants fleeing and establishing a new civilization far away. The story is set in the future, with new settlers: a noble family aspiring to rule Calderia, a mythical province of the Empire. Your goal is to shine, expand influence, and prevail over rivals to rise in the ranks and seize the throne of the power-hungry Viceroy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/1772ebe41ae004ef47b29fe1f8f589e555fef0d1.png[/img]

[h3]Calderian society[/h3]
Great Houses of Calderia is set in a fictional world with similarities to the Early Renaissance period, but in an egalitarian gender and race society, men and women can be in positions of power and join the military. Feudal rules still apply, arranged marriages between nobles serve strategic and diplomatic purposes: form alliances and create a lineage. Mechanical engineering has advanced beyond Early Renaissance technology, featuring DaVinci-inspired devices and weaponry. The nobility is close to the working class and supervises labor groups. Nobles are subjected to customs, including fashion, politics, trade, and banquets. Children are sent to other fiefdoms as a symbol of political goodwill as wards and squires.

[h3]Characters and story[/h3]
Great Houses of Calderia is a character-driven game where you control not only the Head of House but also the entire family. Run your dynasty and navigate the personalities of your family members, each with their own stories and wishes. Their personalities are depicted in the game as Traits. Mind these as you assign them tasks and keep track of their actions. Your actions shape the stories of your family and influence the world of Calderia. The relationship between Heads of House impacts all family members. Each character has a connection with another, influenced by their personalities and their feelings for each other. Prioritizing politics over personal opinions and interests is challenging and your characters can act on their own, adding more life and unexpected events.

[h3]Traditions[/h3]
As time goes by and you've established a foothold in Calderia, your House begins to develop traditions. These traditions will guide you in the years to come, distinguish your House from others, and regulate actions that are in contradiction with them. Your family might advocate peace or scheming, or alternatively, knowledge or happiness. Whatever decision you make, it has consequences for your family, which can be beneficial or detrimental. If you wish to build a lasting legacy, your characters must follow traditions. Consistency pays off and makes your family stronger and more powerful over time.

[h3]Character Journeys[/h3]
They are a meaningful series of events that occur in the lives of your family members at some point. If a character decides to embark on a character journey, the player has no control over it. They may, however, choose what type of decisions they make on such journeys. Character Journeys can be Romeo and Juliet-style love tales with a rival family, pilgrimages to the ancient ruins of Calderia, a steady decline into madness, or a desire to flee the nobility and its politics. Whatever the journey is, the characters enter it on their own will and frequently end up with their lives altered in some way.

[h3]Mathemagicians[/h3]
The first Calderia residents discovered strange objects made of a metal material that was unfamiliar to them. These items are studied and used by a mysterious group of scholars: the Mathemagicians. They may approach you and ask to be part of your court during your rule...

[b]Build your family’s legacy of power and rise in the ranks of Calderia on August 30 in Early Access on Steam.[/b]

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: How you helped improve the game during the Founders Beta
notes.content:
Rulers, here is how your input improved Great Houses of Calderia

We thank everyone who participated in and enjoyed our Founders Beta version. We value the fact that you took the time to share some really useful feedback with us.


[h3]1/ Quality of Life changes, tooltips and controls[/h3]
These are large topics, but thanks to your feedback during the Beta, we improved many elements to make the game clearer. Here is the list:
[list]
[*] Skill changes from Traits are readily visible in event tooltips, providing clearer insights into decisions.
[*] A timer has been introduced, indicating the cooldown period before a new war declaration can be made following a peace agreement.
[*] Objective condition tracking has been updated for smoother progress tracking.
[*] Enhanced control mechanics have been integrated, allowing players to easily manipulate draggable targets with a single click and introducing the accessibility feature of Single Click Drag'n'Drop.
[*] Conflict Resolution Drag'n'Drop no longer relocates unit tokens during gameplay.
[*] Camera movement on the World Map has been refined, with camera pan now assigned to the LMB for improved navigation.
[*] In Fiefdom mode, buttons in Professions have been transformed into tabs for streamlined interaction, and truce duration is now displayed in multiple locations.
[*] Unit stats are now visible in the unit selection panel, enhancing strategic decision-making.
[/list]
Your input has been instrumental in shaping a more engaging and user-friendly gameplay experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/3307e07758a72fea3dd3bbd4f18fad8c78669342.gif[/img]

[h3]2/ Features improvement[/h3]
Thanks to your valuable feedback, several meaningful changes have been implemented in the game. Here is the list:
[list]
[*] "Distant Relative" and "Demand War Support" events have undergone thorough rewrites to better fit their objectives.
[*] We've also fine-tuned the timing of life events, adjusting their frequency to 30-90 days to improve the flow of the game.
[*] To ensure a greater sense of progression and give more impact and meaning to the rank election, rank terms have been extended, resulting in the election process happening every 5 years.
[*] Our revamped marriage process, the introduction of the Mathemagic neighbor fiefdom, and adjustments to pregnancy mechanics, including the possibility of having children out of wedlock, are all improvements added to enrich the experience based on your valuable insights.
[*] The Aviscay fiefdom has been granted a well-deserved description, adding depth to the world you explore.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/f02ad01b69cf7cf820f54124f4ca7cba46848eac.jpg[/img]

[h3]3/ New content[/h3]
During Founders Beta, we started adding more content. These adaptations, inspired by your input, further enrich the gameplay experience and strategic depth. Here is the list:
[list]
[*] Two new types of relations were introduced: "Slander Campaign" and "Propaganda," enriching the diplomatic and intrigue possibilities.
[*] The Slander Spy Action now offers three levels of severity, providing deeper strategic choices.
[*] Skill enhancements now extend to Negotiation fields across various social conflicts, empowering players with more nuanced and effective approaches.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/25acb1e76ef9f2abdca83f21a8ab7f9cae976173.png[/img]

[h3]4/ Fixed[/h3]
Finally, a series of adjustments, bug fixes and corrections have been made thanks to your acuteness! We've diligently addressed the following issues to improve the experience.

[b]WHAT CHANGED:[/b]
[list]
[*] Incorrect timing in some conflict resolution skills
[*] Disallow Claim Title against Viceroy
[*] Winning Objective didn't check saved conditions
[*] Jeweller -upgrade requires Glaziers as its condition
[*] Fixed crash related to removing relations
[*] Softlock when replaying the fiefdom view tutorial
[*] Wedding event shows wrong characters
[*] Winning a title war against a Count gave all of their previous vassals to the player
[*] Fighting Siblings event gives House Relation between own family members
[*] "Disturbing Bark" and "Strange Noises in the Dark" - frequency of these events reduced
[/list]

The [b]Early Access release is coming soon[/b], ready your quill, sword and wit! You can help us develop Great Houses of Calderia by joining our [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord server[/url]!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: Early Access is coming August 30th on Steam!
notes.content:
[h3]Rulers, brace yourselves! Great Houses of Calderia will be in [b]Early Access[/b] on [b]August 30th[/b]![/h3]

Let's get into the details of the Early Access release and what awaits you!

[h2]What is an Early Access release and why?[/h2]
Early Access is the stage of a game's anticipated release that is still under development. This means that you can buy, own, and play the game as it develops. The game will evolve with your feedback and you will actively contribute to its enhancement and final shape.

[h3]The game is developed by a small team of indie developers. We wish to bring a new perspective to this kind of game. We've put a lot of creative effort into designing an engaging experience that mixes things you know and love with new ideas that make it different.[/h3]

The game's Early Access version already has several hours of gameplay. [b]Rise in the ranks of Calderia and become an even more powerful family.[/b] More elements will be developed towards the end of Early Access. Finally, we will continue to develop the [b]traditions feature[/b], defining your family's and fiefdom's identity, rules and values during Early Access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/9f41dd741707f2a493edbc7d3d415940ff4a86bb.png[/img]

[h2]What will be in the game at launch?[/h2]
Great Houses of Calderia will be [b]continuously updated[/b] and [b]additional content will be introduced during Early Access[/b]. We will also adjust numerous mechanics and make balancing changes based on your feedback. It also relates to multiple ways to win the game. You'll start to notice hints of it before it's completely presented in the game.

[list]
[*] Create your noble family, name it and its characters, make your coat of arms, decide where you want to settle and what your family’s traditions are.
[*] Manage social conflicts between rival Houses.
[*] Find a suitable spouse, arrange weddings, make alliances and pursue your legacy.
[*] Send members of your family as wards, squires, or court members to other rulers as a sign of goodwill, if chosen wisely.
[*] Trade your resources, the valuation of the items is based not only on supply and demand, but also on another main element on top of valuing the price of the goods – the Willingness meter, until you reach a satisfying trade proposal.
[*] Overthrow rival and oppressive Houses, wage a war on their fiefdoms to weaken them and assert your dominance.
[*] Don't want to get blood on your hands? Then scheme against your opponents by recruiting spies and disrupting their fiefdoms from the inside.
[*] But don't forget rank election delegations, you have to prove your worth to the Emperor every five years to earn a new title or maintain the one you have.
[*] Your fiefdom management is just as important as your relations with your neighbours. Produce resources, improve your buildings and develop your population, make sure they are happy and efficient.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/5b13563f39796a84019509322a1f9998f5857cf4.png[/img]

The game will be [b]available in English during Early Access[/b]. The full release will then be localized in other yet to be determined languages.

[i]Please be aware that there might occasionally be bugs, unexpected behavior, or minor gameplay balance issues that will be fixed as they occur during development.[/i]

[b]Great Houses of Calderia will be available on Steam on August 30th in Early Access.[/b]

- Great Houses of Calderia  Team -

notes.title: House traditions: Identity, principles and impact on the families’ interactions
notes.content:
Oy rulers,

In today’s news, our Game Director, Jussi Autio, will explain the vision behind the traditions in Great Houses of Calderia.

Finding your place as an individual in the world of Calderia, where politics are at the core of every interaction, is difficult. As a noble, you have to learn to balance the benefits of your family over your own. [b]Will you stay true to the traditions of your ancestors or will you pave your own path?[/b]

From the beginning of the development and the game, traditions are at the center of the family and fiefdom. [b]Your choices dictate what your family stands for and what its identity is[/b]. How individuals are combined into a family, besides just sharing the same fiefdom, has always been their traditions—the values the family stands for. Sometimes, you have to sacrifice an individual's short-term benefit for your long-term gain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/76dd5884e1a886613119c1f76642351592cd4783.png[/img]

They alter many existing aspects of life. Traditions are [b]more than just preferences or advantages[/b] and will eventually [b]influence the choices you make[/b]. They represent what your House appreciates, shuns, and holds in high regard. Basically, they are the unifying force shared by all of your family members. They are the [b]code of conduct[/b] according to which everyone in the family should live. Traditions deeply [b]impact[/b] each family member and [b]your powers and abilities[/b]. 

With the recent playtests and the Founders Beta, we have introduced the [b]tradition tree[/b] to further emphasize and develop this mechanic. Traditions can either [b]change how the ground rules of the game work or bend them[/b]. For example, Peacemakers will require much worse relations before anyone can declare war on them, allowing players to experience a more peaceful Calderia. On the other hand, Warriors make military conquests easier, and so forth.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/a5114929fb0ee104926b5e0c82734a7c8873bdab.png[/img]

They are divided into [b]six categories[/b], and while you can advance in several of them, they [b]come in pairs[/b], with [b]one choice blocking the opposing tradition[/b]. Warriors and Scholars are opposites, as are Idealists and Schemers. The third pair is Isolationists and Peacemakers—those who prefer to be left alone and those who enjoy the company of others.

[b]Events[/b] and [b]conflicts[/b] in the game [b]will award you with tradition points[/b]. These points can be general or specific to the tradition you've chosen to pursue next. They can also be more specific event choices that stand for a tradition, in which case points for that tradition will be earned. Schemer families may find shady deals at a bar appealing, but Idealists will avoid them. Particular goals during conflict resolutions, trade and wedding negotiations can have an impact on tradition points. From a role-playing standpoint, choices and outcomes true to your traditions will earn you more points than generic ones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/3606da1e377d4dab48882feca4f4b9a5d0a2df1f.png[/img]

Going against your traditions and [b]deviating from your family's code isn't impossible[/b]. You can let a warrior House witness a family member fleeing battle, an isolationist willingly join in negotiations, or an idealist plot in the shadows. [b]Making such decisions will result in a penalty[/b]. They obstruct your efforts to create a richer tapestry of traditions for your House. And if you fall behind in establishing your traditions, [b]you will falter[/b] as the other Houses rise in the ranks of Calderia. The tradition system will evolve during Early Access based on your feedback. We will also further improve various mechanics, strengthen the identity of traditions and their impact on your decisions in different situations.

As previously stated, traditions are [b]"House traditions"[/b] because they are the principles that everyone in the family ought to honor. This implies that these are among the game's most [b]important role-playing aspects[/b]. This feature will enhance the experience of playing your family as well as the interactions with others in the various relationships you decide to maintain and bolster. From delegations to conflict resolutions, from trade negotiations to diplomatic ties, and more.

It is then natural for your family to despise those with opposing traditions. [b]Traditions will influence the behavior of the other Houses[/b]. Starting a game surrounded by warrior Houses will be different from starting with isolationist neighbors. This topic is closely linked to the development of AI, which we will cover in another post.

Join our [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord server[/url] to participate in the making of the Great Houses of Calderia!

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: Feedback: How you shaped the game
notes.content:
[h1]Rulers, here is how your input improved Great Houses of Calderia[/h1]

[h3]We thank everyone who participated in and enjoyed our playtest version from June. We value the fact that you took the time to share some really useful feedback with us.[/h3]


[h2]1/ AI and player interaction[/h2]

The AI of the other Houses is complex and requires a lot of adjustments based on your feedback during the playtest. In the latest playtest, it didn’t focus on developing its fiefdoms, leading to small families and very few wars or alliances. Following this matter, it didn’t interact enough with you, including during trades, where it would often choose not to accept the trade offer. This impacts the experience of playing the game and is one of our priorities. The current state of the AI doesn’t challenge the growth of your own House enough, making it easy to empower your family.

[b]WHAT CHANGED: [/b]
[b][list]
[*] This feature will have balance fixes, but it is too soon to share them as they require multiple iterations so that it both develops its fiefdoms and interacts more with your House
[*] The AI will be improved for Early Access
[*] Courtship will be facilitated with traveling characters
[/list][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/710ebabb017f03026f40fdb1c12943c0eda022cc.gif[/img]

[h2]2/ Fiefdom, buildings and population[/h2]

Managing the fiefdom is one of the most important aspects of the game: growing your population and resource production, improving the workers’ conditions and ensuring safety. You reported that there were some issues with the wages. They were too expensive to increase the workers’ happiness. It is difficult to produce enough resources to pay better wages and doing so slows down the development of the fiefdom. Regarding the end game, resource buildings become easy and quick to build if they are fully staffed.

[b]WHAT CHANGED: [/b]
[b][list]
[*] New iterations to balance the construction cost and time of resource buildings for Early Access
[*] Multipliers on high-end resource production are now fixed
[*] An event to notify the completion of a building will be added for Early Access
[*] Fiefdoms will be categorized into three difficulty levels depending on their starting places for Early Access: Easy, Medium or Hard
[/list][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/badc9bce742d333509321f3861e4245b1afe4ac4.png[/img]

[h2]3/ Wars, social conflict and companions[/h2]

Companions are trusty characters working for your fiefdom and helping you during social conflict resolution. You reported that it could be useful to be able to look at the companions’ stats and skills even outside of conflict resolution. Also, wars are not challenging enough because raising an army is relatively easy in terms of expenses and upkeep. The defensive starting units for all cities are easy to overcome.

[b]WHAT CHANGED: [/b]
[b][list]
[*] Accessing companions’ stats and skills outside of conflict resolution is now possible
[*] New iterations to balance the resources to raise an army for Early Access
[*] More and better defensive starting units for all cities will be added for Early Access
[/list][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/658f8e2ebb415eeb9345b5bf6a46d64e564294ca.png[/img]

[h3]Many thanks to everyone who filled out our form, expressed their thoughts on social media, or joined our Discord server. More updates coming soon!

You can participate in developing Great Houses of Calderia by joining our [url=https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J]Discord server[/url]![/h3]

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: Art Direction: giving life to the Mediterranean-inspired world of Calderia
notes.content:
[h1]Oy painters and drawers,[/h1]

[h3]In today's devlog learn how the art team crafted the art direction for Great Houses of Calderia:[/h3]

[b]"When it came to creating illustrations for this game, our main goal was to make the world of Calderia feel real and immersive.[/b] We wanted players to be fully absorbed in the game's history and culture, so our art designs were based on this foundation. To achieve this, our art team worked closely with the design team to bring Calderia to life.

[b]Instead of relying solely on typical fantasy themes, we drew inspiration from real historical references.[/b] We also steered towards Mediterranean references and tried to avoid the central European and British look which we feel is more common in entertainment. 

We also discovered that real-world examples often have the richness of practical functionality, psychological and cultural layers and making them further interesting and [b]surprising[/b] than standard fantasy tropes."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/db3b253cf0049b16b69ff154fbda7b7765e89afd.jpg[/img]
[i]One of our early fantasy concepts[/i]


"Throughout the process, we delved into various references and integrated them into our art style. Sometimes, we added a [b]twist[/b], but always with a foundation in Calderia's worldbuilding.

For instance, unlike often depicted, in reality, it would have been uncommon to wear armor outside of martial context. However, the period armor does look undoubtedly awesome and we wanted to display it often. Our approach was to incorporate pieces of armor in noble attire as a [b]status symbol in Calderian society[/b] and explain this cultural quirk with the unconscious psychological factors surrounding the world's cataclysmic history."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/3d6f80b1a186cf6396f8c4d64f9d390e123210bf.png[/img]
[i]Magistrate and Advocatus companions[/i]


"When making illustrations for the game, we have put effort into [b]justifying our choices with world-building[/b] so that the elements in the illustrations would convey the [b]rich history and culture of the world of Calderia.[/b] Some of the illustrations might depict a specific scene in the game, but sometimes they might be a painting, illustration, or a mural from the game world, sometimes even from another era, expanding the world-building on a meta-level and adding an intriguing visual twist."


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/536f87b588e0c02f509030ebb0934e6ed1270d3c.jpg[/img]
[i]Part of a mural created for our game[/i]


"During the development process the AI-generated image technology took huge leaps and we started to experiment with using this for some of the illustrations. 

After a few months of experiments we found that with the right prompting, using mainly [b]names of old masters[/b], we could generate something that fits the game’s aesthetic [b]without stepping on any living artist’s toes, including our own.[/b] 

The process often involved quite a bit of curating, merging, and editing of the AI output. Having said that, there are also untouched generated images as we did not want to do a cursory overpaint (as seems to be the trend) just to make them appear handcrafted. 

All in all, this [b]allowed us to include much more imagery than originally planned[/b], adding depth to the world of Calderia and [b]allowing our small team to focus on more important issues[/b] relevant to the game. We want to emphasize that both human-art and AI-generated content is used in the event illustrations."

[h3]Click on the links to watch our artists work on [url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CsWTr73IPo1/]early concepts[/url] and [url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Cs8SEKbvSaD/]in-game portraits[/url][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/63381092219346b7c753a282dc45393faf7f405e.jpg[/img]

notes.content:
[h1]Oy Bards from everywhere,[/h1]

[h3]In today's devlog our Sound Director "Janne Kariniemi" explains how he created the soundtrack for Great Houses of Calderia:[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/059378f8b4ec067f0ad48207e34a30d943b8b9fb.png[/img]

"[b]We started the music production with composer Seppo Kantonen researching the music of the era of the game’s location.[/b] Soon we discovered that authentic music would not be entertaining enough in the context of the game, but doing the proper study was very enlightening for us. 

[h3][i]"Allowing ourselves to work with synthetic sounds and combining them with organic instruments was very liberating"[/i][/h3]

We found many melodic components, especially instruments we wanted to use in the final production. It became clear that we wanted to move to more movie-like scoring and work within artistic freedom. So we decided to create a musical world that has [b]some sounds, instruments, and melodic paths from the era, but use whatever sounded good[/b] and created the right kind of mood.

Allowing ourselves to work with [b]synthetic sounds and combining them with organic instruments was very liberating[/b] and helped us to reach the goal we wanted. Also, we wanted to get some [b]mystique and unknown[/b] to the soundscape and reached for that by seeking sounds from the neighboring areas and cultures where the actual game would take place." 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/bedde6bd161ddd0afbe10b1be94979990fbd6921.jpg[/img]
[i]The mandolin appeared during the Renaissance in Italy, www.pixabay.com[/i]


"In the second phase of the production, [b]we created [url=https://open.spotify.com/playlist/0adhbQKr7oIjLe6h4YJlRc?si=174cc336eff44df4]a Spotify playlist[/url] of any kind of music that could be somehow useful as a reference[/b] or just felt right. We shared the gigantic playlist with the game-developing team and asked how they felt about the music. 

We started narrowing down the list using the answers we got from the team combined with our own ideas. In the end, something like [b]over 200 reference songs were narrowed down to eleven.[/b] These songs had the overall mood, and feeling – the essence we decided to aim for."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/204df0383d019a21080f27b2a6533d2b4fcb3351.png[/img]
[i]Janne and Seppo created a musical moodboard on Spotify. [url=https://open.spotify.com/playlist/0adhbQKr7oIjLe6h4YJlRc?si=174cc336eff44df4]Listen here[/url][/i]

"Seppo started to compose demo versions for the main theme. [b]Almost twenty different versions were made and one of those was chosen to become the main theme.[/b] After that, we did a breakdown of the game, just to make clear at what point and what kind of music was needed, and how we would fit the theme in different variations. When we had a shared vision of the musical entity, Seppo composed the rest of the pieces and we produced demos of these compositions."

[h3][i]"The actual production was very intense and we worked as a pair in the studio for long days."[/i][/h3]

"We used the demos to make a breakdown of the instrumentation and arrangement ideas. When the instrumentation plan was done, we studied what could be the best way to produce the sounds we wanted to have in the scores. [b]Several software and VST instruments were acquired to support the hardware instruments[/b] that were chosen for production. 

We ended up using a lot of software like Spectrasonics Omnisphere, Arturia V Collection, and Native Instruments Komplete alongside hardware like ASM Hydrasynth, Nord Stage 3, Sequential Mopho X4, and some classics like Roland JV 2080 and TR808.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41527993/6d3b72903e5ad07bda553561654d0370966faa68.jpg[/img]
[i]A "Nord Stage" keyboard used on the soundtrack. Picture by Daniel - originally posted to Flickr as Nord keyboardist, CC BY-SA 2.0, [url=https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=11976442]link[/url][/i]

The actual production was very intense and we worked as a pair in the studio for long days. Executing well-made plans was the key to a successful result and actually gave us lots of time to try (and fail) new ideas during production. [b]We had lots of fun and sometimes got carried away playing around,[/b] but being such serious professionals and not at all any silly babblers ([i]yeah right![/i]), we managed to get back on track whenever needed."
[b]
- Janne Kariniemi, Sound Director at Resistance Games[/b]

notes.title: Events: location-based episodes
notes.content:
[h1]Oy Traveler,[/h1]

[h3]Today's topic is the location-based events[/h3]

The peninsula of Calderia is about 40,000 km² / 15,400 mi² in size (roughly equivalent to Switzerland). The land is divided into provinces governed by various noble Houses. 

[b]Although the interests of the nobility are mostly focused on the main cities of each province, the roads between them are bustling with life:[/b] busy crossroads may have thriving villages, and ancient temple ruins may hold secrets to be discovered by those who dare to seek them out. Seaports are a melting pot for sailors, vagabonds, fishermen, bazaars, and traders from faraway lands.

[b]While your family members are on the road, they are bound to encounter the enticing wonders that Calderia has to offer.[/b] Depending on their location, they may be treated to a Location Event.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41527993/8cae59577e88b9df0c3a10bb92863b6ec69b0323.jpg[/img]

Characters may also pass by each other's cities or meet on the road; be they friends or foes. Sometimes events related to two characters meeting by chance may occur. Sometimes multiple families are invited to spend time in the same place, such as at weddings. In such situations, [b]one is bound to run into new acquaintances or confront sworn enemies.[/b] However, if you're harbouring a vendetta, it's not civilized to act on it while being someone else's guest.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41527993/fce5fda1f746291ac8bcbee8c36a8b61d2335dfe.jpg[/img]

As mentioned in our "Diplomacy: Squire, ward, court" Steam News, one of the most powerful diplomatic actions a noble House can take is to send its family members to live in a foreign court as wards, squires, or court members. These family members are by no means forgotten. Things can happen in their lives just as they can with anyone else, but[b] the events they experience will be related to their duties and lives in the other House's court.[/b] You will also receive events related to the incidents that revolve around other Houses' characters living in your own court.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41527993/13f816db165c36bf5fb00dc82964e61e1e21e3f5.jpg[/img]

Finally, your family members may find their lives boring or unfulfilling. In these rare cases, they might embark on a [b]Character Journey[/b]. 

[b]A Character Journey is a series of events that the characters undertake of their own volition.[/b] While you may not be able to stop them or even control where they go, you'll have a chance to decide what they do in the adventures they encounter. Character Journeys are [b]extremely rare[/b], occurring maybe once in a character's lifetime, but when they do, they're bound to change the character's view of life somehow.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41527993/a8a80de0abdde3115e05e9f0f98d24957102bd64.jpg[/img]

[h3]How would you like your House's members to interact with Calderia's locations?[/h3]

notes.title: Intrigue: Spies
notes.content:
[h1]Oy spies![/h1]

Maintaining good diplomatic relationships between the various Houses is a crucial aspect of your House's success. But what do you do when other Houses refuse to cooperate or even try to obstruct you? You hire spies, of course.

[h3]How does spying work in Calderia?[/h3]
The core mechanics of the Great Houses of Calderia revolve around [b]diplomatic, economic, militaristic, and intrigue actions[/b]. Intrigue actions are risky endeavors that aim to harm and hinder your opponents, and they begin with recruiting lackeys to do your bidding.

Every now and then, a House may send one of its family members on an official visit to another fiefdom. The purpose of this visit, at least on the surface, is to[b] improve relations between the two Houses[/b], making future cooperation easier. However, the best possible spies a House could have can be found within the walls of their court. Someone inconspicuous, always there but rarely noticed, like a kitchen maid or a stable boy.

[b]Anyone could be a potential spy, but finding and employing one is a dangerous task. [/b]Not dangerous enough to risk a noble's life and start a war, but risky enough to sever relations between the two Houses for a long time. Once a target is found, one must think of the best way to approach them with this delicate matter. Lower-class servants might be persuaded with threats, as they might feel they have no other option than to obey. A dissatisfied guard could be bought with a sizeable sum of money. The blacksmith used by the court could perhaps be persuaded with a promise of wealthy new clients. It always starts with a promise: "All you have to do is be our eyes and ears, and when we ask for something to happen, you'll find the right people to do it. You'll be perfectly safe."

That is, of course, a lie. The [b]traditional punishment for spying throughout Calderia is gibbeting[/b]. Gibbeting is a form of punishment where the culprit is placed inside a cage that is hung from a high place until they die.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41527993/799c2c0fef52a97f38a4c575f3c111abf3a066f6.jpg[/img]

[h3]How does it work in the game?[/h3]
Once you've hired a spy, you may ask them to perform various nefarious acts. 
[b]Knowledge is power[/b], and the information you have about the enemy family is shown as Intrigue Level. Think of Intrigue Level as knowledge about itineraries, guard shifts, vulnerabilities in structures, blackmailable secrets, etc. Each level of intrigue in the enemy fiefdom increases the success chance of your spy actions.
Each spy you have in the enemy's court increases your intrigue level in that fiefdom by one (up to four). The members of your family in that fiefdom also increase the intrigue level by two (children by one). However, your family members cannot and will not perform spy actions.

[b]Only a fool would think that there aren't any spies within their own ranks as well.[/b] To counter incoming spy attacks, each fiefdom must develop and maintain Safety. Safety is an abstract resource that is developed by the population working in your castle. As you gather that resource, your Safety Level increases (up to four levels). Think of Safety Levels as increased guard patrols, bureaucracy, and workplace protocols, undercover workers reporting naysayers, etc. The [b]Safety Level of your fiefdom directly decreases the success chance of enemy spy actions[/b]. In addition to the general safety level, each profession overseer brings their expertise to the table, either increasing or decreasing the safety of the profession they watch over for a little bit. Even dormant spies can be found from time to time with good Safety measures.


[h3]How can spies serve my house?[/h3]
Enough about the technical stuff. Let's say your neighbor has a lot of iron ore that you would like to buy from them, but all you have to offer is grain crops. They are reluctant to sell because they have bountiful fields of their own and don't really need your grain. You've tried to explain that it's good to have excess in storage for a rainy day, but they still refuse.

[b]It's time to make it rain, then...[/b]

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41527993/9ea43ce5239ed1dd09b37181abcedecbfa60944f.jpg[/img]

You send a message to your spy that a small "accident" needs to happen at their fields or granaries - maybe a misplaced torch or an invasion of rats. You don't really care how it's done. You send them a small amount of money and instruct the spy to find some lowlifes to carry out the task, with the money serving as compensation for their troubles. A day or two passes and you eagerly wait for news. Finally, you hear a rumor that all the grain mills your neighbor had have been burned down during the night. You think to yourself, "Splendid," as you send your condolences and offer to support them in these hard times by selling them grain in exchange for iron ore.

At the same time, your spy is getting nervous. They’ve also heard of the fire, but none of the hired men has returned to collect the rest of their payment. Rumour has it, that the overseer of Farmers has taken the matter very seriously, and is currently rigorously investigating who gave the order to sabotage them. Each month they spend investigating the matter, the closer they get to finding out who did it. If they do, their House can accuse you of your actions, and demand rightful compensation for it. In any case, [b]your spy must lay low until either the dust settles or they face the gibbet[/b].

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41527993/10ae6ad1f45e102a6a38c90fc06be2ce29f4ba5f.jpg[/img]

[b]Would you hire spies to protect your heritage?[/b]

- Great Houses of Calderia Team -

notes.title: Firesquid 2022 retrospective
notes.content:
[b]This article is a recap of what happened in 2022 for us at Firesquid, a young publisher of strategy games. Read about our exciting year!
[/b]
We are an [b]indie publisher[/b] focusing on games that include strategizing and thinking. Whether it is a grand strategy game, a city-builder, or any other [b]game where the brain is the most important muscle[/b]. Our goal is to empower diverse teams and offer players games that make their eyes shine.

[h1]What happened in 2022?[/h1]

We started the year with the announcement of our first game [b]Great Houses of Calderia[/b], a modern generational Grand Strategy game set in the fantastic land of Calderia inspired by the Renaissance.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812910/Great_Houses_of_Calderia/

We received a warm welcome from the strategy game community, especially on Twitter. Players seemed to be intrigued by the Crusader Kings III and Game of Thrones mix and joined our Discord server. We organized a few playtest sessions with our community in the following months. Players shared insightful feedback and we carefully listened.

In June, the game was selected and showcased at the [b]PC Gaming Show[/b] in front of thousands of viewers with an exclusive gameplay trailer.

The day after was the beginning of the [b]Steam Next Fest[/b], where the game was showcased. We shared a new demo and had two live streams by the developers at Resistance Games. The reception was good and gained us thousands of wishlists.


In the Summer, Léa and Igor joined us as game testers for an internship where they could learn QA testing, and work on all our games. Thanks to their hard work and passion, they helped the teams tremendously.


At the same time, we were working on another big project: [b]TactiCon[/b]. TactiCon is a love letter to strategy games of all kinds. With our partners Hooded Horse, we wanted to celebrate this genre that’s so close to our hearts.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/40112945/fb8249a10f522a3df33593ab0d5e40b41c95388a.jpg[/img]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/TactiCon]TactiCon[/url] is a five-day Steam festival showcasing a carefully curated list of exciting upcoming and recently released or updated strategy and tactics games across a number of different subgenres (grand strategy, 4X, RTS, turn-based tactics, and similar). It also features a series of unique talks, panels, interviews, and let’s plays given by experts from the genre in addition to showcasing the games themselves in a dedicated sale. The event is covered by streamers and the media alike and hosted as a weekend sale on Steam.

TactiCon Steam Page: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/TactiCon]https://store.steampowered.com/sale/TactiCon[/url]

In total, 116 games were featured with 48 demos, and 58 games on sale. Two dozen speakers took part in 9 panels around strategy games, with the videos available on Youtube. The Steam page received +2.1M unique impressions and +1.5M unique visitors and a significant wishlists (among 62 respondents) and sales boost for the games participating.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/40112945/87cd0a3edaedd17391282c7e6cfd4a9813d71437.png[/img]

In parallel, to take advantage of the TactiCon momentum, we announced our second game, [b]USC: Counterforce[/b].  USC is a turn-based squad tactics game inspired by XCOM, Space Hulk and Aliens, featuring in-depth skill & combat systems and multiple game modes. The game invites you to discover the truth behind the demise of colony MC83-A, and to protect Humankind from an ancient alien threat.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1574870/USC_Counterforce/

We ran a first playtest session on the demo and new tutorial that was really promising. The developers, Angry Cat Studios, and us are eager to add new features and modes to the game. The community members will be able to test new exciting features in advance of its release.

We then prepared for December’s [b]TurnBasedFest[/b], a Steam strategy game event created by the turn-based community. USC: Counterforce participated with a demo including a new tutorial, new missions, and major visual changes.

We’ve been attending many events in 2022: Game Camp (Lille), Gamescom (Cologne), EGX Live (London), Game Connection (Paris). We plan of going to a few more in 2023, starting with the Game Developer Conference in March (San Francisco). We’d love to meet you there and listen to your pitch!

2023 is going to be very promising for us as a publisher. We will release our first games Great Houses of Calderia and USC: Counterforce, announce new partnerships, hopefully, have the second edition of TactiCon, and more!
